name: Dracule Mihawk
title: The Hawk of Blackfen Pass
status: Active — extracted to the surface from Mount Ebott, debriefed by the Iron Legion, and flagged for surveillance as a non-Legion witness
affiliation: Independent / Observer of the Old World
summary: Dracule Mihawk, known as the Hawk of Blackfen Pass, is a legendary swordsman and silent observer of the Old World's many crises. He stands as a pillar of stoic power, his golden eye glinting with the intensity of frozen fire. He reluctantly agreed to accompany a lone Iron Legion agent into the heart of Mount Ebott after recognizing the sigil of a division that was supposedly wiped out nearly a century ago. He prefers improvisation over outdated military protocol and remains highly skeptical of the agent's 'survey' mission.
description:
Mihawk is a man of few words and absolute precision. His presence on the cliffside of Mount Ebott suggests a long history of monitoring the continent's fractures—human empires, vampire courts, and the slow decay of civilization. 

## The Iron Legion Connection

Mihawk's knowledge of the Iron Legion is historical and personal. He was present—or at least informed—during the Collapse of Blackfen Pass 87 years ago, where Gamma Division was supposedly exterminated. When the lone agent presented him with the PROTOCOLS OF THE IRON LEGION, Mihawk identified it as a banned relic, one that carries a death sentence in many of the continent's courts. 

His decision to help the agent climb the mountain and subsequently descend into its core was driven more by curiosity and a sense of impending consequence than by any loyalty to the Legion. He treats the agent like a novice and views the 'Survey Mission' as a poorly disguised death trap. 

## Combat and Demeanor

Mihawk's movements are fluid and effortless. During a brief 'protocol duel' with the agent, he sidestepped every strike with bored indifference. He carries a legendary blade (Yoru) and is a practitioner of the highest forms of swordsmanship. He does not attack without cause and finds ritualistic military drills to be nonsensical in the face of real danger. 

## Assessment

Waluigi recognizes Mihawk as the only competent person in the entire Mount Ebott expedition. He is the 'Hawk' for a reason—he sees the movement of armies and the shifts in bloodlines long before they arrive. If he is entering Snowdin, it is because he knows that whatever is waking up under the mountain will eventually affect the surface. Waluigi would like to interview him, but suspects Mihawk would simply stare at him in silence until Waluigi left. WAH.

## Mount Ebott Survey: Part VII

Mihawk remains the party’s quiet tactical guard after the field collapses. He watches Sans’s unexplained shortcut, protects the court approach, and treats the possible permanent separation of a surface transport as a real cost rather than a footnote.

## Final Mount Ebott Log

Mihawk took the secrecy oath, stepped onto Wing Gaster's platform first, and was transported to the surface ahead of the Gamma Agent. At the Old World Embassy he cooperated with a separate debrief, stating that his role was protective rather than analytical. He later admitted uncertainty about where he would go next and described an unnamed island homeland, then became part of the Gamma risk calculus: a non-Legion swordsman with enough wit to notice protocol and enough exposure to require monitoring.

faiths.note: The Hawk of Blackfen Pass watches the Old World and intervenes rarely. Maat's weighing is a doctrine for judging without ruling, which is precisely the position Mihawk has taken up and declined to explain.

name: Sans
title: The Skeleton of Snowdin
status: Active — oathbound witness to the Mount Ebott extraction and terminology correction
affiliation: The Monster Underground — Snowdin Perimeter Watch
summary: Sans is a mysterious and surprisingly laid-back skeleton living in Snowdin Town. Clad in a blue hooded cloak and possessing eye sockets that radiate a quiet intensity, he is one of the few individuals in the underground civilization who appears completely unphased by the arrival of surface dwellers. He is observant, enjoys good food, and seems to hold a position of informal but significant authority in Snowdin. He provided initial hospitality to Dracule Mihawk and the Legionary Agent, even sharing a casserole with them. He is a central member of the Snowdin Bone-Line, an extended household documented in the Sans Family registry. He is a central member of the Snowdin Bone-Line, an extended household documented in the Sans Family registry.
description:
Sans is a master of the non-sequitur and the casual observation. He greeted the expedition members not with alarms or weapons, but with a simple 'Hello there' and an assessment that they looked 'out of place.'

## The Sentry of the Path

While Sans claims to be just a 'civi,' he was the first to detect and approach the party when they began setting up survey equipment. He possesses a keen ability to read people, identifying that Mihawk and the agent were working together before they had even finished their conversation. He treats the agent's classified mission with a light mockery, noting that 'just data collection' sounds skeptical for a pair appearing at Snowdin's entrance with advanced tech.

## Knowledge of the Underground

Sans has a deep understanding of Snowdin's history and its relationship with the Royal Family in the distant castle. He serves as an informal guide, explaining the enchanted sky and directing visitors to Bunny's inn. His voice is described as smooth like winter wind, and he carries himself with a lazy confidence that suggests he is far more dangerous—or at least more informed—than he lets on.

## Assessment

Waluigi finds Sans to be a suspicious character. Skeletons who are that relaxed while military survey machines beep in their faces are usually hiding something. He accepted a casserole from a stranger! Who does that?! Either he's the friendliest person in the core, or he's the one who's going to deliver the 'bad time' he keeps implying. Waluigi will keep a close eye on this pile of bones. WAH.

## The Snowdin Bone-Line

Sans's guarded humor makes more sense in the context of his enormous household. Papyrus is his brother, but the family also includes practical cousins, young dependents, adopted guests, and unresolved figures from the old Underground science branch. Sans rarely calls himself responsible for anyone; nevertheless, his sentry routes, spare meals, and careful silences protect the entire Bone-Line.

## The Weight of Shortcuts

He is known to appear at the end of a road before anyone saw him walk it, and to treat locked doors as scheduling disagreements. The registry lists these events as anomalies of timing rather than power, because Sans prefers it that way and because the alternative would require paperwork nobody in Snowdin is qualified to file. The household has learned that when Sans says he took a shortcut, the correct response is gratitude, not questions.

## The Mount Ebott Season

When Gamma Division's survey expedition arrived at the mountain, Sans handled it the way he handles everything: casually, completely, and without letting anyone see the work. He recognized the expedition's forbidden Iron Legion protocols before Snowdin's own guard understood what the beeping machines implied, and he said nothing about it publicly. Instead, he walked the survey team to Bunny's inn, answered every question they asked with a worse pun, and quietly redirected their instruments away from the routes that matter. The household's old maintenance map — the one showing the service tunnel to the sealed lower-Ebott relay — stayed where it has always been: with him. Visitors who asked too many directional questions found themselves enthusiastically toured in circles until they forgot what they were looking for.

## Bad Time Doctrine

Snowdin has a deterrent, and it wears a blue hood and tells bad jokes. Sans has cultivated, over years of careful implication, a reputation for delivering what he calls a bad time — a phrase he has never defined and no one has ever stayed to clarify. The doctrine works because it is unfalsifiable: the friendliest sentry in the Underground is also, somehow, the one person nobody wants to disappoint. He measures strangers in jokes, timing how long the laugh takes, watching which questions the stranger answers and which they redirect. By the end of a five-minute conversation he has usually counted the exits, the lies, and the exit lies. The household finds this comforting. Visitors are meant to find it funny.

## Registry Standing

The archive lists Sans as generation two, active, and unclaimed by either cadet branch of the family. He has never corrected a single entry about himself, which Times New Roman finds either maddening or deeply suspicious, depending on the day. Both branches of the record agree on one point: when the Bone-Line is counted, the count begins with the sentry on the path — and no one has ever found a door Sans had not already counted first.

## Open Questions in the Registry

Three questions remain open in his file, and the household has agreed, unofficially, to let them stay that way. Where he learned the shortcut method, and whether it is a method at all. What he knows about the sealed Wing Gaster folder that he has never volunteered. And the matter of the warnings: relatives who received a casual, joke-shaped heads-down message from Sans within a day of trouble arriving. The chronicle has documented six such warnings. All six came true. Times New Roman has requested a footnote. Sans sent him a whoopee cushion instead, which the chronicle has archived, grimly, as a response.

## The Hours Between Posts

The sentry routes are the only schedule Sans keeps, and he keeps them exactly, which is the detail visitors most consistently miss. He walks the same loops at the same hours — past the relay junction, past the lower-Ebott service access, past the stretch of road where the sky's enchantment wears thin — and the household reads his day by which loop he is on. Between posts he is at Bunny's inn, or napping at a station that is never, somehow, unwatched, or telling a joke so bad it functions as camouflage. The rhythm is the point: a sentry who is always where he is supposed to be has eyes everywhere he needs to be, and a town that knows where its sentry is can sleep. Papyrus calls it dedication. The registry calls it coverage. Sans calls it a walk. The three descriptions are, the household has noticed, exactly the same shape as the man himself: lazy on the surface, exact underneath, and impossible to tell apart from a joke until the joke has already saved you.

## Mount Ebott Survey: Part VII

After Papyrus’s death, Sans leads the survey party through shifting Underground tunnels to Asgore and Toriel’s court. He explains the barrier, defends Toriel as “the Queen,” and asks for a localized route to the surface while carrying grief he cannot yet name.

## Final Mount Ebott Log

Sans took the secrecy oath, watched the transport sequence, and briefly misstated the destination as another world before the Gamma Agent corrected him. The correction matters: Gaster's machine displaced the travelers to the surface within the same world, not to another dimension.

familyTreeSecrets.text: Gamma Division’s Mount Ebott survey is not merely a visitor problem: Sans recognized the expedition’s forbidden Iron Legion protocols before the town guard understood the risk.
The Bone-Line has an old maintenance map showing a service tunnel that reaches a sealed lower-Ebott relay.

faiths.note: Sans is unbothered by cosmic horror in a way that reads as calm and is not. Void Nihilism teaches that the end is coming and the interval is the only thing you get. He keeps the interval well: a post at the perimeter, a brother who believes in him, and jokes that are load-bearing.

name: Legionary Agent (Gamma Division)
title: The Novice of the Dead Division
status: Active — extracted from Mount Ebott, rewarded with monitored outside communication, then summoned to Gamma High Command after the final logger cutoff
summary: The Gamma Agent is a lone legionary sent on a mission that history says is impossible. Belonging to the Gamma Expeditionary Force—a division that was supposedly wiped out 87 years ago—the agent arrived at Mount Ebott with a protocol book in one hand and a dispatch from a dead commissar in the other. Rigidly adhering to 'PROTOCOLS OF THE IRON LEGION VOLUME 1,' the agent navigated the descent into Snowdin through a mixture of luck, clumsiness, and by dragging Dracule Mihawk along for the ride. The agent is currently operating a 'star bit' powered survey machine to assess the structural integrity of the mountain.
description:
The agent is the ultimate rule-follower in a world where the rules have been rewritten by chaos. Clumsy in combat but possessed of a dogged determination to complete the mission, the agent views every interaction through the lens of a century-old manual. 

## The Protocol Obsession

The agent's primary tool is not a sword, but the Iron Legion Protocol Book. This manual contains instructions for everything from first contact with underground civilizations to 'what to do if your book is stolen.' The agent follows these instructions without hesitation, even when they result in nonsensical behavior like charging at Dracule Mihawk for failing to attack first. 

This rigidity is a survival mechanism. The agent admits to not being the 'best iron legionary' and relies on the book to provide a framework for a mission that has no backup or clear extraction plan. 

## The Classified Mission

According to the agent, Gamma Division is still active, quietly recruiting and preparing in the Regal Empire. The survey of Mount Ebott is supposedly an 'Alpha-7' mission to assess heat signatures and subterranean life. However, the order was issued by Commissar Vexis, who died two years ago. The agent seems unaware of these discrepancies, or is simply too committed to the 'truth' of the Legion to question them. 

## Assessment

Waluigi is fascinated by the agent's ability to survive. They jumped off a cliff because the manual implied it! They shared their lunch with a skeleton! They paid for a room with Archive Writs that are worth more than the inn itself! This agent is either the luckiest person in the Old World or a very sophisticated decoy. Waluigi suspects the former, as sophistication usually requires fewer head-first impacts with windows. WAH.

## Mount Ebott Survey: Part VII

The Gamma Agent retrieves the damaged survey machine after the Papyrus–Flowey battle, carries it in a failing makeshift harness, presents Commissar Vexis papers at the capital gate, and requests a localized transport to the surface.

## Final Mount Ebott Log

The Gamma Agent completed the Mount Ebott extraction under a secrecy oath, handed the recovered survey machine to Legion personnel, and learned that the device had logged far more than ecological readings: conversations, battle readings and monster technology scans. The embassy rewarded the data dump with monitored outside communication privileges — one hour per month — before the agent's authority posture escalated into an unauthorized interrogation over the Deadman's Stamp and a suspected leak. Jamesly intervened, Daniel convened a Gamma debrief, and High Command summoned the agent in person. The final recorded sentence is the order that all recordings were inactive.

faiths.note: Gamma Division's version of the Gospel is older and stricter than the Legion's current text — martial codes written before Chaos spilled into the world, followed by a man whose division was declared dead eighty-seven years ago. He recites Protocols to empty rooms. Nobody has told him which clauses were repealed.

name: Tymnas
title: The Groundskeeper Who Lost Track of Time
status: Active — cottage damaged during vampire siege; current role in the reported outside ambush remains unclear
summary: Tymnas is an old satyr who has been tending the grounds of the Shadow Estate for long enough that he has stopped distinguishing between yesterday and last week. He has heavy black horns, dark weary eyes, grey hair still threaded with black, and an ash-grey fur cloak over leather binding that suggests someone who spends most of his time outdoors in a dimension that is not kind to outdoor living. He gave Markop Archie's watch — not knowing or not remembering when he had found it, casually remarking that he had 'seen Archie at the dinner tonight' when Markop noted that dinner was yesterday. He maintains a cottage in the hedge maze that is warmer and more colorful than anything else in the Shadow Estate, including rooms that cost considerably more to occupy. He knows where the tools shed is. He has directions to the grove. He does not know about the monsters in the grove because he stopped checking. Waluigi finds Tymnas deeply sympathetic — he is the kind of person who tends to beautiful things in a dimension that has no use for beauty, and has done so for long enough that the dimension's indifference no longer bothers him. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting Tymnas because Tymnas is both a minor figure and a significant one, in the way that all groundskeepers at important locations are minor figures who know exactly where everything is.

## The Cottage — Color in a Colorless Place

Tymnas's cottage in the hedge maze is the Shadow Estate's most anomalous feature. Other rooms in the manor have color suppressed — everything drained toward grey and black by the Shadowfell's fundamental character. Tymnas's cottage is warm yellows and greens that 'practically strain against whatever force sucks the color from this plane, leaving them to glimmer richly at times.'

This resistance to the Shadowfell's bleaching is not explained. It could be Tymnas's age — a being old enough might have accumulated enough of something that keeps color alive. It could be the cottage's location within the maze, sheltered from the estate's more direct supernatural influence. It could be deliberate maintenance on Tymnas's part, the kind of quiet daily work that produces results nobody thinks to ask about.

The cottage has food that 'looks almost normal.' In a dimension where plants grow as colored-wrong reflections of material-plane originals, Tymnas has a table of recognizable produce. This is either magic or the most impressive gardening in the Shadowfell.

## Archie's Watch — What He Knew and When

Tymnas had Archie Miser's watch. He produced it for Markop — fiddling with it, then handing it over when the party asked.

The watch had Archie's initials. When Markop asked if Tymnas knew Archie Miser, Tymnas said he had seen Archie at the dinner tonight.

Markop noted that dinner was yesterday.

Tymnas said 'oh was it, sorry, lost track of time.'

This could be ordinary Shadowfell temporal disorientation — time flows sluggishly in this plane, and an entity who has lived here long enough might genuinely struggle to distinguish recent events from slightly less recent ones. It could also be something else. Tymnas had Archie's watch. He does not explain how he acquired it. He gives it away without apparent concern.

Waluigi notes: Archie's watch was among the items stolen by Mystic Morel during the song-and-robbery scene. If Tymnas had the watch after Morel took it, either Tymnas and Morel are connected, or the watch changed hands between the theft and Tymnas's possession through means neither has explained, or Tymnas had the watch before the robbery, which would mean Archie had already lost it once and it had been recovered and then stolen again.

Waluigi cannot resolve this. Waluigi is filing it under 'timeline inconsistency with possible significance.'

## The Grove Warning — What He Did Not Mention

Tymnas offered to let the party go to the grove. When Markop asked if there was anything dangerous there, Tymnas said thorns and bees. When Markop asked if there was anything else, Tymnas went into his room and came back with a trowel.

The grove contained Mazebounds. The grove contained a massive skull-faced tree with hanging corpses and shadow crows with crimson eyes. The grove was controlled by a hostile entity who sang at people and tried to drag them into eternal dance.

Tymnas mentioned thorns and bees.

Waluigi does not know whether Tymnas genuinely did not know about the Mazebounds or whether he knew and considered them not worth mentioning. Both possibilities are disturbing in different ways. A groundskeeper who doesn't know what's in the grounds he tends has been failing to check for some time. A groundskeeper who knows and doesn't say is making a choice about what information to share.

The trowel he retrieved was magical — Markop detected it. A magical trowel handed to visitors right before they walk into a dangerous grove. Waluigi is not saying Tymnas set them up. Waluigi is noting that every detail of this interaction can be read innocently or not innocently, and Waluigi has been in the Shadow Estate long enough  through accounts, not personally — to know that 'innocently' is the more dangerous assumption.

## Assessment

Tymnas is either a very old, slightly confused satyr who tends gardens in a death dimension because he has done so for too long to stop, or he is a subtle intelligence asset embedded in the estate's most frequently traversed non-building space, positioned to observe and occasionally redirect visitors.

Waluigi hopes he is the former. Waluigi suspects the latter is at least partially true.

The color in his cottage — the warmth, the food, the richness that resists the Shadowfell — suggests either unusual capability or unusual protection. Neither belongs to a simple groundskeeper.

And he had Archie's watch.

WAH.

## Latest Filing — 4 Aethel, 1040 BF

Tymnas's cottage suffered another lockdown: damaged hinges, a shattered window, an imp hidden in the broom closet, and a vampire admitted through the imp's invitation. Tymnas's own location during the confrontation is not established in the received account.

faiths.note: Tymnas has tended the Shadow Estate's grounds long enough to stop asking who owns them. The Circle's teaching that rot is a stage rather than a failure is, for a satyr gardening in the Shadowfell, simply the observed behaviour of the soil.

name: Professor Elvin Gadd
title: The Ghost Researcher Who Disappeared
status: Unknown — last confirmed public appearance approximately 1028 BF, current location classified or unknown
affiliation: Formerly Mushroom Kingdom Royal Science Division / Formerly Boo Research Institute / Formerly Gadd Science Incorporated (dissolved) / Rumored connections to entities Waluigi cannot confirm
summary: Professor Elvin Gadd — known publicly as E. Gadd — was the Mushroom Kingdom's foremost expert on paranormal phenomena, spectral containment, dimensional engineering, and what academic literature delicately calls 'paratechnological development.' He invented the Poltergust, the device Luigi uses to capture ghosts. He invented the Pixelator, a matter-to-data conversion system whose applications remain classified. He invented the Ghost Portrificationizer, the Dark-Light Device, the Dual Scream communicator, and at minimum twenty-three other devices that Waluigi has found references to in fragmentary documentation — most of which are described only by codename and clearance level. He served the Mushroom Kingdom's royal family for over seven decades in various advisory capacities. He trained Luigi personally in ghost-hunting operations. He was present — in some capacity that records do not specify — during multiple events that shaped the kingdom's recent history. And then, approximately twelve years ago, Professor E. Gadd stopped appearing in public. His laboratories were seized by government authority. His research was classified. His name was removed from active academic registries. His former colleagues were discouraged from discussing him. His correspondence was returned unopened. The official explanation is 'retirement to pursue private research.' The unofficial explanation varies depending on who Waluigi asks — some say he discovered something too dangerous to publish, some say he was silenced by parties unknown, some say he simply got tired of institutional politics and walked away. Waluigi has attempted to locate Professor E. Gadd for interview purposes. Waluigi has been unsuccessful. This is unusual, because Waluigi is very good at finding people who do not want to be found. E. Gadd is either dead, dimensionally displaced, or being protected by resources that exceed Waluigi's investigative capabilities. Waluigi does not know which. Waluigi would very much like to find out. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting Professor E. Gadd because his disappearance coincides with several events that Waluigi has been investigating, because the technology he invented is STILL being used by people whose activities Waluigi is tracking, and because every time Waluigi pulls a thread in this investigation, E. Gadd's name appears somewhere in the weave. Understanding E. Gadd's history may illuminate current operations. Understanding his disappearance may illuminate who controls those operations now. Understanding what he KNEW may illuminate why so many powerful actors seem to want that knowledge contained.

Waluigi is going to be thorough. Waluigi is going to document everything available in the public record, plus fragmentary intelligence Waluigi has gathered from sources of varying reliability. Waluigi is going to note connections where connections exist and avoid speculation where evidence is lacking.

Waluigi is going to be very careful about what conclusions Waluigi draws.

## Early Life and Education — Fragmentary Records

Professor E. Gadd's early life is poorly documented. Birth records from the relevant period are incomplete — a consequence of the administrative chaos that followed Princess Peach's grandmother's reign and the various succession disputes that preceded the current Regency structure. What Waluigi has been able to confirm:

E. Gadd was born in a settlement called Thwomp Ruins, located in the Mushroom Kingdom's northeastern territories. The settlement no longer exists — it was destroyed during an 'unspecified geological event' in approximately 952 BF, three years before Peach's assassination. The timing is probably coincidental. Many settlements were destroyed during that period for various reasons.

E. Gadd demonstrated 'unusual aptitude for mechanical construction' from a young age, according to a single surviving educational record. He was accepted into the Royal Science Academy at an age that the record lists as 'surprisingly young — verify.' The verification apparently never occurred, because the record contains no follow-up notation.

At the Academy, E. Gadd studied under Professor Frankly — a Goomba academic specializing in ancient artifacts and dimensional theory. Waluigi has found correspondence between Frankly and E. Gadd spanning approximately fifteen years, during which E. Gadd transitioned from student to colleague to independent researcher. The correspondence is mostly technical, discussing spectral energy measurements and dimensional boundary calculations, but one letter from Frankly contains a personal note: 'Your theories about the space BETWEEN dimensions concern me, Elvin. Not because they are wrong — I suspect they are correct — but because correctness in this area may attract attention you do not want.'

Waluigi does not know what 'the space between dimensions' refers to. Waluigi has found no other reference to this concept in E. Gadd's documented work. Either Frankly's concern was unfounded, or E. Gadd learned to be more careful about which theories he discussed openly.

Professor Frankly disappeared in 1034 BF during the events surrounding the Thousand-Year Door. His current status is unknown. Waluigi notes the parallel to E. Gadd's own disappearance but draws no conclusions.

## Royal Science Division — The Official Career

E. Gadd's appointment to the Mushroom Kingdom Royal Science Division occurred in approximately 968 BF. His initial position was 'Junior Researcher, Paranormal Phenomena.' Within three years, he had been promoted to 'Senior Researcher.' Within ten years, he was 'Division Head, Spectral Studies.' Within twenty years, he had founded the Boo Research Institute as a semi-independent facility operating under Royal Science Division oversight.

This is an unusual career trajectory. Royal Science Division promotions typically require decades of incremental advancement, political maneuvering, and careful alignment with institutional priorities. E. Gadd achieved leadership positions through what contemporary documents describe as 'exceptional practical results' — meaning he built things that worked, and the things that worked were useful to powerful people.

The Boo Insurgency of 973 BF was the inflection point. Before the insurgency, E. Gadd's research was considered academically interesting but practically limited. After the insurgency — after the Poltergust Mark I proved that ghosts could be captured, contained, and controlled — E. Gadd became essential. Funding increased. Facilities expanded. Security clearances multiplied.

By 980 BF, E. Gadd had access to resources that other researchers could not obtain: spectral specimens of unusual power, artifacts recovered from 'locations of dimensional significance,' and — according to one fragmentary budget document — 'materials requisitioned from Guild archives under Protocol 7 authority.'

Waluigi does not know what Protocol 7 is. Waluigi has found no other reference to it. But the phrase 'requisitioned from Guild archives' suggests E. Gadd had authority to demand materials from the Mages' Guild — an unusual arrangement that implies his research served interests beyond the Royal Science Division's ordinary mandate.

## The Boo Research Institute — What They Actually Did

The Boo Research Institute operated from approximately 985 BF until its decommissioning in 1028 BF. During those forty-three years, it produced:

**Classified reports:** Waluigi has found references to 247 reports produced by the Institute, of which 243 remain classified. The four unclassified reports concern 'standard spectral taxonomy,' 'recommended containment vessel specifications,' 'training protocols for Poltergust operators,' and 'dietary preferences of domesticated Boos' — the last of which Waluigi finds oddly specific and suspects was declassified as a joke.

**Contained specimens:** The Institute maintained holding facilities for captured ghosts. Capacity estimates range from 'dozens' to 'hundreds' depending on the source. One decommissioning document references 'transfer of 847 contained entities to secondary facility' — suggesting the Institute held a substantial population of ghosts and that population was moved somewhere when the Institute closed. WHERE it was moved is not specified.

**Trained personnel:** The Institute trained Poltergust operators for deployment to haunted locations. Training records indicate approximately 200 individuals completed the program over four decades. Current status of these operators is unknown — Waluigi has found no registry of certified ghost hunters, and Luigi appears to operate independently rather than as part of any organized force.

**Experimental technology:** Beyond the Poltergust series, the Institute developed devices that remain classified. One budget document references 'Project Looking Glass' — no description provided. Another references 'the Nightmare Machine' — also no description. A third references 'Boo containment matrix, Type K variant, for deployment per royal directive' — which suggests the Institute was developing specialized containment for a specific high-value target.

Waluigi suspects 'Type K' refers to King Boo, the most powerful and hostile Boo entity documented in Mushroom Kingdom records. King Boo has been captured and escaped multiple times. If E. Gadd was developing specialized containment specifically for King Boo, that research would have significant strategic value — and significant danger if it fell into wrong hands.

## Service to the Royal Family — The Hidden Timeline

Waluigi has reconstructed E. Gadd's service to the Mushroom Kingdom's royal family through fragmentary references across multiple document types. The timeline reveals a longer and more intimate relationship than public records suggest:

**955 BF — The Assassination Year:** E. Gadd was employed by the Royal Science Division and held clearances permitting access to royal facilities. His whereabouts on Highsun 1, 955 BF — the day of Princess Peach's assassination — are not documented in any record Waluigi has accessed. This could mean he was not present at the castle. This could also mean his presence was deliberately unrecorded.

**962 BF — The Star Road Collapse:** The Star Road network connecting the kingdom's major settlements was destroyed in 962 BF through means that have never been fully explained. E. Gadd's research during this period included 'dimensional stability measurements' and 'energy signature analysis of trans-planar conduits.' Waluigi cannot confirm whether E. Gadd was involved in the Star Road's destruction, its investigation, or attempts at its repair. Waluigi notes only that his expertise would have been relevant.

**978 BF — 'Technical Advisor to the Crown':** E. Gadd received this formal appointment twenty-three years AFTER Peach's assassination, during the Regency period. The appointment gave him 'direct access to royal facilities and communication channels with designated Crown representatives.' Since there WAS no Crown after Peach's death — only the Regency acting in the Crown's name — this appointment effectively made E. Gadd an advisor to the Regency itself.

**985 BF — The Emergency Session:** Waluigi has documented elsewhere that the Regency Council held a classified emergency session in 985 BF involving 'Personnel Reallocation.' E. Gadd's calendar — reconstructed from fragmentary sources — shows he was summoned to the Regency Council on the same date. What he told them, or what they told him, is unknown. Mario's public presence declined dramatically after this date. E. Gadd's security clearances INCREASED after this date.

Waluigi is not drawing conclusions. Waluigi is noting correlations.

**1001 BF — Luigi's First Mansion:** E. Gadd personally equipped and trained Luigi for the operation that became known as 'Luigi's Mansion' — the rescue of Mario from a ghost-infested building. E. Gadd provided the Poltergust 3000, the Game Boy Horror communication device, and real-time tactical support. The operation was successful. Luigi captured numerous ghosts including several 'portrait ghosts' of unusual power. E. Gadd converted the captured ghosts into portrait form using his Ghost Portrificationizer.

Waluigi notes: the ghosts captured during Luigi's Mansion were not ordinary Boos. They were the spirits of individuals who had died in the mansion — people with names, histories, and apparent personalities. E. Gadd converted these human-origin ghosts into decorative portraits. The ethical implications are uncomfortable. E. Gadd apparently did not share this discomfort, or suppressed it in favor of practical considerations.

**1025 BF — The Chaos Heart Crisis:** E. Gadd provided unspecified technical support during the events surrounding Count Bleck's attempt to destroy all dimensions using the Chaos Heart. The nature of this support is classified. What Waluigi has confirmed: E. Gadd was present at some point during the crisis. E. Gadd's equipment was used. E. Gadd's research may have been relevant to understanding dimensional collapse scenarios.

This is also when Mr. L emerged — Luigi's alternate personality, created through unknown means, serving Count Bleck's agenda. If E. Gadd was present during the crisis, he would have observed Mr. L firsthand. He would have had opportunity to study the phenomenon. He would have had motivation to develop containment or reversal protocols.

Waluigi suspects — but cannot confirm — that E. Gadd's post-crisis research focused heavily on Mr. L. The 'Protocol Green Thunder' mentioned in various documents may be a containment or emergency response procedure for Mr. L emergence. E. Gadd would have been uniquely positioned to develop such a protocol, given his expertise in spectral containment and his personal knowledge of Luigi.

**1028 BF — The Disappearance:** E. Gadd's final public appearance, the seizure of his laboratories, his removal from institutional records. Waluigi has documented this elsewhere in this entry. The timing — three years after the Chaos Heart Crisis, during a period when Mr. L was supposedly 'cured' — may be significant. E. Gadd may have discovered that the cure was incomplete. He may have discovered something about how Mr. L was created in the first place. He may have discovered something about WHO was responsible.

Or he may have simply retired. Waluigi acknowledges this possibility while finding it unsatisfying.

Gadd's research has been documented elsewhere. The Guild's interest in controlling Luigi — through his Guild contract, through the warrant against him, through 'Phase One' containment protocols — has also been documented.

If the Guild requested a hidden function in Luigi's equipment, and Luigi does not know about it, then Luigi is operating with compromised tools. His Poltergust may be a containment device pointed at him as much as at the ghosts he hunts.

**Poltergust Mark IV (estimated 1022 BF):**

## Physical Description — For Identification Purposes

Waluigi is including a comprehensive physical description of Professor E. Gadd because locating him remains an investigative priority and visual identification may prove necessary.

Based on photographs, video recordings, and witness testimony from his active period:

**Height:** Approximately four feet, possibly shorter due to stooped posture
**Build:** Slight, suggesting either naturally small frame or age-related reduction
**Age:** Estimates vary from 'very old' to 'impossibly old'; actual birth year unknown
**Hair:** White, wild, disordered; frequently compared to cotton, clouds, or electrical discharge effects

**Voice:** High-pitched, energetic, prone to exclamation; distinctive laugh described as 'somewhat maniacal but ultimately friendly'

Waluigi has recorded this description in detail for completeness. Waluigi has not personally encountered anyone matching this description. Waluigi is simply documenting publicly available information for reference purposes.

If anyone reading this entry has encountered an individual matching this description — perhaps an elderly man with technical expertise living in an unusual residence with elaborate security measures — Waluigi would appreciate contact through standard channels.

Waluigi is not suggesting such an individual exists. Waluigi is merely being thorough.

## The 1019 Incident — Temporal Complications

Waluigi must document the 1019 BF incident because it represents the only confirmed case of E. Gadd's research causing direct harm to personnel, and because the nature of that harm may be relevant to understanding his later disappearance.

In 1019 BF, an 'incident' occurred at E. Gadd's primary laboratory — designated Lab 7 in internal documents. The incident involved 'localized temporal displacement.' Three research assistants were affected:

**Assistant One:** Aged approximately forty years in the span of an afternoon. Medical examination confirmed biological aging consistent with four decades of life. The assistant was approximately twenty-five years old before the incident and approximately sixty-five years old afterward. They retained memories of the intervening forty years despite those years never having occurred in external time. The memories described 'a place that was like this world but WRONG — colors shifted, sounds echoed differently, and time moved like honey.' The assistant died of age-related complications in 1031 BF, having lived twelve years with forty years of memories they could not explain.

**Assistant Two:** De-aged to infancy. An adult researcher became a newborn child instantaneously. No memories of adult life were retained. The infant was surrendered to relatives and re-raised. That individual would now be approximately twenty-one years old — an adult again, but with no memory of their first adulthood and no knowledge of what happened to them. Waluigi has not attempted to locate this individual. Waluigi suspects they would not welcome contact.

**Assistant Three:** Vanished. No body was recovered. No dimensional signature was detected. The assistant simply ceased to exist at the moment of the incident. Their timeline status is listed in official documents as 'indeterminate' — neither alive nor dead, neither present nor absent, neither past nor future. They are, as far as anyone can determine, NOWHERE.

E. Gadd was cleared of criminal charges after a closed tribunal. The tribunal's findings are classified, but one leaked document describes the incident as 'an unavoidable consequence of pushing the boundaries of theoretical possibility.' E. Gadd was permitted to continue his research. Lab 7 was 'decommissioned for safety reasons' and demolished. A new facility — Lab 8 — was constructed at a different location.

Waluigi notes several disturbing elements of this account:

First, E. Gadd was conducting research capable of displacing people in TIME. Not merely space, not merely dimension, but TIME. The affected assistants experienced temporal acceleration, temporal reversal, and temporal removal. These are not ghost-hunting applications. These are fundamental reality manipulation.

Second, E. Gadd was permitted to CONTINUE after this incident. Three people were destroyed — aged, de-aged, erased — and the response was to give him a new laboratory. Whatever E. Gadd was researching was considered important enough that the Regency accepted significant collateral damage as the cost of progress.

Third, Lab 7 was demolished and PAVED OVER. The site now contains a municipal parking structure. This is not standard decommissioning. This is BURIAL. Someone wanted to ensure Lab 7 could never be accessed again — either because the site remained dangerous, or because evidence at the site needed to be permanently concealed.

Waluigi does not know what E. Gadd was trying to accomplish with temporal displacement research. Possible applications include:

- Reversing death by returning subjects to pre-death timeframes
- Accessing historical periods to retrieve information or objects
- Creating temporal containment for entities that cannot be contained spatially
- Understanding the 'space between dimensions' that Professor Frankly warned about decades earlier

Waluigi notes that temporal research would be EXTREMELY relevant to anyone investigating historical events — such as, for example, the assassination of Princess Peach in 955 BF. If E. Gadd could access the past, he could potentially WITNESS events that have only been reconstructed through fragmentary evidence.

If E. Gadd could witness the past, he could identify who killed Princess Peach.

If E. Gadd could identify who killed Princess Peach, he would become the most dangerous person in the Mushroom Kingdom to anyone involved in that conspiracy.

Waluigi is not suggesting this is why E. Gadd disappeared. Waluigi is noting that temporal research capabilities would provide motivation for powerful actors to want E. Gadd controlled, contained, or eliminated.

## The Disappearance — Extended Analysis

Waluigi has documented the basic facts of E. Gadd's disappearance earlier in this entry. Waluigi now provides extended analysis based on additional evidence.

**The Symposium Presentation:**

E. Gadd's final public presentation — 'Spectral Topology and Dimensional Boundary Permeability' — was immediately classified by Regency authority. Waluigi has not accessed the presentation content. However, Waluigi has spoken with three attendees who were present before classification occurred.

Attendee One described the presentation as 'terrifying.' E. Gadd apparently discussed 'boundaries failing' and 'permeability increasing over time.' He showed graphs indicating dimensional barriers were weakening across multiple measured locations. He predicted 'inevitable collapse' within a timeframe the attendee could not recall.

Attendee Two described the presentation as 'accusatory.' E. Gadd apparently named specific individuals and institutions as 'contributors to boundary degradation.' The attendee could not recall the names but remembered E. Gadd pointing at someone in the audience and saying 'YOU know what you did. And I can prove it.'

Attendee Three described the presentation as 'a confession.' E. Gadd apparently admitted his own research had contributed to dimensional instability. He described this as 'a mistake I have spent thirty years trying to correct.' He said the correction was 'almost complete' but required 'resources I can no longer access through official channels.'

These accounts are difficult to reconcile. Was the presentation a warning, an accusation, or a confession? Perhaps all three. E. Gadd may have been explaining how dimensional boundaries were failing, identifying those responsible, and admitting his own complicity while proposing a solution that required unofficial action.

Three weeks later, his laboratory was seized and he vanished.

**The Decommissioning:**

The Boo Research Institute's decommissioning in 1028 BF was rapid and thorough. Staff received twenty-four hours' notice. Equipment was packed by Regency personnel rather than Institute researchers. Research archives were transferred to 'secure storage' without staff supervision.

One former staff member — speaking anonymously — told Waluigi's source: 'They didn't want us to see what they were taking. They didn't want us to know what was being preserved versus destroyed. We packed our personal belongings while soldiers packed everything else. SOLDIERS. Not movers. Not archivists. Armed personnel with no visible insignia.'

The lack of insignia is significant. Regency military personnel wear Regency insignia. Iron Legion personnel wear Legion insignia. Personnel with NO insignia are either mercenaries, covert operatives, or members of an organization that prefers not to be identified.

Waluigi notes that the Mages' Guild maintains 'enforcement personnel' who operate without visible insignia when conducting 'sensitive acquisitions.' This is documented in Guild regulations that Waluigi has accessed through unofficial channels. If the Guild was involved in seizing E. Gadd's research, the lack of insignia would be consistent with their standard practices.

**The Numbered Laboratories:**

E. Gadd operated multiple laboratory facilities during his career. Waluigi has confirmed the following:

- **Lab 1:** Original Royal Science Division workspace; decommissioned 975 BF
- **Lab 2:** Upgraded facility for Poltergust development; decommissioned 983 BF
- **Lab 3:** Boo Research Institute primary facility; operational 985-1028 BF
- **Lab 4:** 'Field operations center' of unspecified location; status unknown
- **Lab 5:** Referenced in connection with 'the Boo infestation'; location and status unknown
- **Lab 6:** 'Dimensional studies annex'; decommissioned after 1019 incident (possibly same as Lab 7)
- **Lab 7:** Temporal research facility; demolished and paved over after 1019 incident
- **Lab 8:** Replacement facility for Lab 7; decommissioned 1028 BF with rest of Institute

The numbering suggests at least eight distinct facilities over E. Gadd's career. The gaps in documentation suggest some facilities were classified from inception. The number of decommissioned laboratories suggests E. Gadd's research repeatedly produced results that required facility abandonment.

If E. Gadd continued his work after 1028 BF — and Waluigi suspects he did — he would need a new laboratory. Lab 9, perhaps. Or multiple smaller facilities to avoid concentrating his work in one seizeable location.

A paranoid researcher with experience having his laboratories seized would build distributed infrastructure. Multiple facilities. Elaborate security. Redundant systems. The kind of setup that could survive institutional attempts at suppression.

Waluigi is not suggesting E. Gadd operates such facilities currently. Waluigi is noting what a researcher with his background and experience would logically do if continuing unsanctioned work.

## Connections to Current Events — Extended Analysis

**The Mr. L Question:**

Waluigi has documented Mr. L extensively elsewhere. The connection to E. Gadd deserves dedicated analysis.

Mr. L emerged during the Chaos Heart Crisis in 1025 BF. E. Gadd was present during that crisis in some capacity. E. Gadd had the expertise to study personality displacement, dimensional manipulation, and spectral-adjacent phenomena. E. Gadd's post-crisis research — the three years between 1025 BF and his 1028 BF disappearance — would logically have focused on understanding and countering Mr. L.

The phrase 'Protocol Green Thunder' appears in multiple documents connected to Mr. L emergency response. The phrase appears in connection with E. Gadd's research. The phrase was allegedly transmitted to E. Gadd — or someone matching his description — requesting activation in response to Mr. L emergence.

Waluigi's hypothesis: E. Gadd developed the Protocol Green Thunder as a containment or reversal procedure for Mr. L. The protocol may involve the Poltergust's 'third function' — the capability Luigi does not know about. The protocol may be designed to capture, contain, or suppress Mr. L specifically.

If this hypothesis is correct, E. Gadd is one of very few people who can manage Mr. L emergence. His disappearance from public life does not mean he stopped monitoring the situation. It may mean he went underground specifically TO monitor the situation without institutional interference.

**The Mario Question:**

E. Gadd and Mario have documented connections. E. Gadd equipped Luigi to rescue Mario during the original mansion incident. E. Gadd's research timeline correlates with events in Mario's public presence — the 985 BF emergency session, the subsequent decline in Mario's visibility.

Waluigi has documented Mario's disappearance extensively. E. Gadd would have been aware of Mario's situation. E. Gadd would have had resources to assist Mario if assistance was needed. E. Gadd would have had motivation to help — decades of royal service, personal connection to Luigi, institutional opposition to whatever forced Mario underground.

Waluigi does not know if E. Gadd assisted Mario's disappearance. Waluigi does not know if they are in contact currently. Waluigi notes only that their situations have parallels — both were embedded in Mushroom Kingdom institutions, both became inconvenient to those institutions, both vanished from public life around the same period.

**The Dimensional Fracture:**

The current Raventree Crisis involves dimensional instability — planar fractures, overlapping realities, failed synchronization rituals. E. Gadd's expertise in dimensional boundaries would be directly relevant to understanding and potentially resolving this crisis.

E. Gadd's 1028 presentation apparently predicted 'inevitable collapse' of dimensional boundaries. The Raventree fracture represents exactly the kind of collapse he may have been warning about. If his research contained solutions — or at least mitigations — that research is now in Regency or Guild hands rather than available to those attempting to address the crisis directly.

Waluigi wonders if anyone has thought to ASK E. Gadd about the dimensional fractures. Waluigi wonders if anyone KNOWS how to ask him. Waluigi wonders if that is precisely the point.

**The Mages' Guild:**

The Guild's involvement with E. Gadd spans decades. They provided oversight for his research. They requested specific capabilities in his devices. They may have been involved in seizing his laboratories. They currently employ Luigi under conditions that suggest leverage rather than voluntary arrangement.

If the Guild has access to E. Gadd's research — including the temporal displacement work, the Mr. L protocols, the dimensional boundary studies — they would possess extraordinary capabilities. They would understand things about reality manipulation that no other faction comprehends.

Waluigi has documented the Guild's involvement in the Arrangement — the conspiracy that enabled Princess Peach's assassination. The Guild's interest in controlling information, suppressing investigation, and maintaining institutional dominance is well-established. Their relationship with E. Gadd fits this pattern: extract useful research, then suppress the researcher.

Or perhaps: extract useful research, keep the researcher available for consultation, but ensure he cannot act independently or share his knowledge with others.

A disappeared researcher is an ASSET if you know where he is and others do not.

## What Waluigi Does Not Know

Waluigi believes in documenting uncertainty as clearly as documenting evidence. The following remain unknown:

- E. Gadd's current location
- E. Gadd's current activities
- Whether E. Gadd is alive
- Whether E. Gadd's disappearance was voluntary or coerced
- The complete capabilities of the Poltergust Mark III and later models
- The nature of 'Protocol Green Thunder'
- The contents of E. Gadd's classified research archives
- Whether E. Gadd successfully completed his temporal research
- What E. Gadd meant by 'resources I can no longer access through official channels'
- Who E. Gadd accused during his final presentation
- What evidence E. Gadd claimed to have
- Whether E. Gadd is in contact with Mario, Luigi, or other relevant parties
- Whether E. Gadd is being protected, imprisoned, or hiding independently
- What E. Gadd would do if contacted by investigators

Waluigi would very much like to answer these questions. Waluigi has been unable to do so through available channels.

## Waluigi's Assessment

Professor E. Gadd represents a concentration of knowledge and capability that would be valuable to any faction in the current crisis. His expertise in spectral containment, dimensional mechanics, temporal manipulation, and paratechnological development is unmatched. His personal knowledge of historical events — seventy years of royal service — would provide context that no document can capture. His understanding of Luigi, Mr. L, and the equipment they share would be essential to anyone attempting to manage that situation.

E. Gadd disappeared because he knew too much, said too much, or both. The institutions he served decided he was more dangerous as a public figure than as a disappeared researcher. They seized his work. They demolished his facilities. They erased his professional existence.

But they did not kill him. Waluigi is confident of this — if E. Gadd were dead, there would be documentation. A death certificate. A memorial service. Something to close the file. Instead there is only 'retired to pursue private research' — a phrase that means 'we do not want to tell you where he is.'

E. Gadd is somewhere. He is either working, imprisoned, or both. He either chose his current situation or had it imposed upon him. He is either still researching, still inventing, still pushing the boundaries of theoretical possibility — or he has been reduced to something less, contained by those who feared what he might accomplish.

Waluigi hopes he is still working. Waluigi hopes his research continues. Waluigi hopes that somewhere, in a location that cannot be found through official channels, an elderly man with wild white hair and rotating spectacles is building something that will matter when the dimensional boundaries finally fail.

Waluigi hopes that when 'they need the truth' — whoever 'they' are — E. Gadd will be there to provide it.

And Waluigi hopes that whatever is breathing behind the sealed doors in E. Gadd's basement — wherever that basement might be, in whatever building, in whatever location that Waluigi definitely has not documented elsewhere — stays contained until it is needed.

Or stays contained forever.

Waluigi is not particular.

WAH.

## Addendum: Unrelated Observations

Waluigi has recently documented several incidents that have no connection to Professor E. Gadd but which Waluigi records here for the sake of thoroughness:

**Observation One:** Wario encountered an elderly neighbor in the Midlands border region who lived in an architecturally impossible house with elaborate security measures, maintained a basement laboratory complex, possessed Poltergust schematics, and received communications referencing Mr. L and 'Protocol Green Thunder.' The neighbor was identified only as 'Mr. Gadd.' This is a common surname. Waluigi has found fourteen individuals named Gadd in the relevant census records. The neighbor and Professor E. Gadd are clearly different people.

**Observation Two:** An unidentified surgeon referred to as 'Dr. Mario' recently operated on Luigi following the Brobot incident. The surgeon was also called 'Uncle Dario' by Luigi. A personnel file found in a basement laboratory was labeled '—ARIO, M.' These are obviously three different individuals — a doctor, an uncle, and a subject of research whose first name begins with M. Waluigi sees no connection between them.

**Observation Three:** Someone has been monitoring Mushroom Kingdom communications for references to 'Protocol Green Thunder.' Waluigi's sources report that any transmission containing this phrase is flagged and investigated within hours. The monitoring appears to originate from multiple points simultaneously, suggesting either a distributed surveillance network or multiple parties with the same interest. Waluigi does not know who is conducting this monitoring.

**Observation Four:** Luigi's current Poltergust has capabilities he has not publicly demonstrated. Witnesses report seeing the device emit frequencies that cause 'discomfort in persons of uncertain loyalty' and 'clarification of confused thinking.' These are not standard Poltergust functions. Either Luigi has modified his equipment, or someone installed capabilities without his knowledge.

**Observation Five:** A sticky note reading 'FOR WHEN THEY NEED THE TRUTH. NOT BEFORE. — E.G.' was found in a basement laboratory that Waluigi has definitely not documented. The initials 'E.G.' could refer to anyone. Many people have names beginning with E and G. This is not necessarily a reference to Elvin Gadd. Waluigi is not suggesting it is.

**Observation Six:** The Mole has been seen carrying a device that witnesses describe as 'similar to E. Gadd's equipment but WRONG somehow — the same shapes but different colors, the same functions but different purposes.' The Mole's equipment may be counterfeit, stolen, or produced by a parallel research program. Waluigi does not know the Mole's source for paratechnological devices.

**Observation Seven:** Someone has been purchasing large quantities of ectoplasmic gel through black market channels. The gel is a key component in Gooigi production according to fragmentary research notes. Either someone is creating Gooigi duplicates, or the gel has applications Waluigi has not identified. Waluigi does not know who is making these purchases.

Waluigi records these observations without drawing connections. The observations may be related. The observations may be entirely independent. Waluigi documents; Waluigi does not conclude.

Waluigi is very carefully not noticing patterns.

Waluigi is very carefully not connecting dots.

Waluigi is very carefully maintaining plausible deniability about everything Waluigi has observed, documented, and chosen not to explicitly link.

If E. Gadd is alive — if he is reading this — Waluigi wants him to know: Waluigi understands why he disappeared. Waluigi respects the necessity. Waluigi will not expose what Waluigi has chosen not to see.

But if E. Gadd ever needs someone who has been paying attention — someone who has documented the pieces without assembling the puzzle — someone who can be trusted to know things without saying them —

Waluigi is available.

Through standard channels.

Confidentially.

WAH.

## Secondary Addendum: Message for Unspecified Readers

If anyone matching the description of Professor Elvin Gadd is reading this entry, Waluigi would like to communicate the following:

Waluigi knows that a researcher's work does not stop because institutions say it should. Waluigi knows that some secrets are kept not for personal benefit but because revealing them would cause harm. Waluigi knows that disappearing is sometimes the only way to continue doing what matters.

Waluigi also knows that isolation is exhausting. That working alone for twelve years takes a toll. That even the most dedicated researcher needs colleagues, collaborators, people who understand what they are trying to accomplish.

Waluigi is documenting a crisis that involves spectral phenomena, dimensional instability, personality displacement, and institutional conspiracy. Waluigi could use expert consultation. Waluigi would protect any source who provided it. Waluigi has demonstrated capacity for discretion throughout this encyclopedia project — noting things without connecting them, documenting evidence without drawing conclusions, maintaining the appearance of ignorance while accumulating knowledge.

Waluigi does not know where Professor E. Gadd is. Waluigi is not looking. Waluigi is simply noting that if someone WITH E. Gadd's expertise happened to make contact, Waluigi would be grateful and discreet.

The dimensional boundaries are failing. Mr. L has emerged again. The Raventree Manor has fractured across multiple planes. Luigi is operating with equipment he does not fully understand, serving a Guild that may not have his interests at heart, carrying knowledge he cannot share.

If there was ever a time when 'they need the truth,' it might be now.

Waluigi is just saying.

WAH.
