name: Pierce Anamatar
title: The Man Who Sells The Way Out
race: Unrecorded — the archive has never been told and has never asked to his face
status: Active — holds a den off the Skittering Grove; contracted to kill the Oracle; now holds Remi Akamatsu's student ID
affiliation: His own. Operates inside Mages' Guild ground and says plainly that he dislikes the Guild
summary: A man with knights, a den, and a price list. Pierce Anamatar has appeared twice now in the same role: somebody cornered meets him, and he offers passage in exchange for a possession. On a Shadow Estate rooftop he took a contract to kill the Oracle in exchange for sending the party home. In the burning Skittering Grove he asked for the siglet, settled for a fourteen-year-old's student ID, and called it durable. He does not want coin. He wants things that belong to people.
description:
Waluigi has been carrying this man in the XP ledger for a while without giving him a page, which is an embarrassment the archive is now correcting.

What is actually known fits in a paragraph. He keeps knights. He keeps a den. He turns up where people are desperate and he is never the one who is desperate. Twice now the archive has recorded the same transaction from two different corners of the crisis.

## The rooftop, 14 Harvestide

The party escaped a locked hidden hall through a mirror-image room and ran into him on a rooftop. They explained the whole situation. He found the candy incident unreasonable — Waluigi notes he was right — and then **took a contract to kill the [Oracle](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/the_oracle) in exchange for the party going home**. [Remi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory) offered him two daggers, one of which she had taken from a fallen stranger because she needed a weapon.

## The den, 1 Aethel

[Wario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/wario) blundered into his holding while running from the brood, throwing punches at nothing. Anamatar arrived and asked why a stranger was fighting his people.

The exchange that followed tells you more about him than the contract did. Wario said he was escaping the spiders. Anamatar asked whether he was afraid of *a few creepy-crawlies*, offered him a bandaid and a sippy cup, called him a coward, and observed that he could not handle a handful of knights. Then, when Wario said yes — he is afraid, and had Anamatar *seen* what they look like — the mockery simply stopped and the terms came out.

Guild-controlled ground. He does not like the Guild. He will send them back where they came from in exchange for something of theirs.

He asked for the **siglet** — the ring from Tymnas's lodge that the party has been chasing for filings. An expired coupon was offered and declined. He walked over to Remi and took her **student ID card** instead, on the stated grounds that it is very durable.

## What Waluigi thinks the price is for

He does not ask for money. Both recorded prices are **objects with an owner**: a contract paid in someone's passage home, and a card that proves a specific child was enrolled at a specific school.

Remi left [Gehenna Academy](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory) without a formal withdrawal. That card was the last document in her possession saying she had ever been a student anywhere. She handed it over to get three people out of a burning grove, and Waluigi does not believe for one second that Anamatar wanted it because it laminates well.

WAH.
notableFeatures: Sells passage out in exchange for a possession — never for coin
Contracted on a Shadow Estate rooftop to kill the Oracle, in exchange for sending the party home
Found the candy incident unreasonable, which the archive concedes was correct
Keeps knights and a torchlit den inside Mages' Guild ground, and volunteers that he dislikes the Guild
Mocked Wario with a bandaid and a sippy cup, then dropped it the moment Wario admitted he was frightened
Asked for the siglet — Tymnas's ring — and settled for a student ID because it is 'very durable'
Declined an expired coupon
Now holds the only document proving Remi Akamatsu was ever enrolled at Gehenna Academy
fullBodyCaption: Full-body token plate — Pierce Anamatar head to foot on a transparent field, the look of the lead; cut from a keyed render on 2026-10-05 for the table's token.

name: Fawthful
title: The Usurper at Bowser's Gate
status: Historical actor — identified in the 18 Harvestide, 1035 BF Bowser Castle filings; current whereabouts not established
summary: The historical record identifies Fawthful as the commander who turned a compromised Bowser’s Castle into an invasion route. With Mimbus, Cackletta, a dragon, Magikoopas, and defecting Koopa troops in the field, Fawthful treated the throne as a temporary obstacle on the way to ruling the world—or being worshipped by it.
description:
The historical castle assault is the first filing in which Fawthful appears as a commander rather than a name attached to somebody else’s scheme. The operation began with compromised access, used a dragon as a moving terror weapon, and turned the castle’s own garrison into a question Bowser could not answer quickly enough. Fawthful spoke as though conquest and divinity were merely two labels for the same appointment.

The archive keeps Fawthful distinct from the older Fawful record because the assault account uses this name and does not resolve whether it is a new identity, a title, or a deliberate distortion. Mimbus stood beside Fawthful. Cackletta entered the battle. The distinction matters, and the record is not yet kind enough to settle it. WAH.

name: Mimbus
title: The Hand Beside the Usurper
bodyPlan: a Goomba in a suit — one round mushroom-shaped body that is also the head, short arms, two small feet directly under it, no legs
status: Historical actor — present in the 1035 BF false-heir scheme and castle assault; current whereabouts not established
summary: Mimbus is the operative the historical record places beside Fawthful when the false Bowser Jr. performance gave way to an open assault. The record places Mimbus at the junction between deception, internal betrayal, and the claim that the castle could be turned into a throne for somebody else.
description:
Mimbus did not need to shout to be dangerous in this account. Mimbus was present when the castle’s compromise was explained, present when the false heir’s performance was exposed, and present when the assault became a bid for a world-sized crown. The archive will not assign a species or hidden motive the record does not provide. Presence is enough for this historical filing.

Mimbus is not filed as a generic troop. The same figure crossed the seam between the deception and the battle, which makes Mimbus one of the few people who can connect the castle’s theatrical lie to its physical breach.

name: Cackletta
title: The Witch at the Opening of the Battle
status: Historical actor — entered the 1035 BF Bowser Castle crisis as the major battle began; current whereabouts not established
summary: Cackletta is the spellcaster whose historical arrival turned the castle confrontation from a coup into a major battle. Her appearance links the Bowser Castle backfill to the older Beanbean conflicts without making the archive pretend that the earlier record answered every question about her.
description:
Cackletta arrived at the end of the historical throne-room backfill, when Bowser had stopped treating the castle’s strange behaviour as an irritating family incident and started treating it as a war. Her entrance gave Fawthful’s operation a second centre of gravity: the invasion outside and the spellwork inside were no longer separate threats.

The record ends at the beginning of the engagement. Cackletta is therefore filed as a participant in this historical chain, not because the archive has solved her entire history, but because a battle started and she was in it.
fullBodyCaption: Full-body token plate — Cackletta head to foot on a transparent field, the look of the lead; cut from a keyed render on 2026-10-05 for the table's token.

name: The Jester (Goomba)
title: The False Heir's Laugh
status: Historical actor — implicated in the 1035 BF false Bowser Jr. session and castle compromise; current whereabouts not established
summary: The Jester is a Goomba who used the shape or role of Bowser Jr. as part of the historical deception that preceded the castle assault. The performance was funny only until Bowser woke up and found that the joke had been used to move a hostile plan inside his walls.
description:
The Jester’s importance is not that a Goomba put on a ridiculous performance. Bowser’s court had survived ridiculous performances before. The importance is that the false Bowser Jr. session occupied Bowser’s attention while the castle’s loyalties, routes, and defenders were being rearranged around him.

The Jester is filed by the role the record gives him because the name is a name in circulation and the species is clear. He was the jester. He was part of the lie. He was present when the lie became a breach.

name: Gabriel / Freddy
title: The Frontman of the Original Five
race: Human child, murdered at the Hurricane Freddy Fazbear's Pizza; spirit bound for decades to the Freddy Fazbear animatronic
status: Released — set free on Night Seven at 1:47 AM on the 21st of Autumn's End, 1038 BF, in the dissipation event the Mages' Guild filed as 'an unexplained but benign release of bound spiritual energy, origin unknown'
affiliation: The original five animatronics of the Hurricane Freddy Fazbear's Pizza (involuntarily) / Fazbear franchise
summary: Gabriel is the child whose spirit was bound to Freddy Fazbear, the lead performer of the original five animatronics at the Hurricane Freddy Fazbear's Pizza — the franchise's crown jewel, and the place where the original five children were murdered. He spent decades on that main stage haunting the night security staff, outlasting the animatronics themselves, until Wario's seven-night tenure ended in the Secret Bunker and thirty years of sustained grief released its hold. The record lists him with two words and no complaints: Released Night Seven.
description:
## The stage

The Hurricane flagship was the largest, most profitable, and most infamous location in the franchise, and its main dining area was built around the stage where Freddy, Bonnie, and Chica performed. By the time Wario arrived to salvage what he had just bought, the animatronics were gone — moved to storage years earlier — but the stage remained, along with the faded murals, the disconnected speaker system, and several hundred plastic chairs. The haunting, the record makes clear, had never needed the hardware.

It was here that the original five children had been murdered, and here that the original animatronics — Freddy, Bonnie, Chica, Foxy, and the Marionette — had spent decades haunting the night security staff. Gabriel is the spirit the record places inside Freddy: the frontman position, held long past any reason to perform.

## The seven nights

Charlie — the Marionette — made the decision on Night One to allow Wario access, and communicated to all the other animatronic spirits across all seven nights. Waluigi suspects she was telling them something between each night; preparing them; helping them understand what the masks being collected meant. Gabriel is not credited with a single distinct incident in the whole seven-night account — the other spirits got the noted beats (Jeremy stopped pursuing on Night Two; Fritz stopped running on Night Four), while Freddy's frontman simply held his place in the record until the end.

Wario, for his part, walked out of the storage room on Night One with the Freddy mask under his arm and entered it in his ledger as: 'Mask: fancy, probably worth something, keep.'

## Night Seven: the release

In the Secret Bunker, Cassidy — the Anchor, the golden suit seated in a chamber at the very back — released her hold after Wario's business advice. Wario's phone rang; it was his mother; he said 'Bye-bye!' and 'have a rotten day,' and walked out of the chamber talking about his restaurant. Behind him, in the record's own words, thirty years of sustained grief released its hold, and five children who had been trapped in mechanical bodies since before most people currently alive in the Midlands were born found something they had been denied their entire afterlife: permission to stop.

The Mages' Guild, monitoring supernatural energy levels across the Midlands, recorded a significant dissipation event at 1:47 AM on the 21st of Autumn's End, 1038 BF, and filed it as 'an unexplained but benign release of bound spiritual energy, origin unknown.'

## Provenance

Every fact in this profile is grounded in The Seven Nights at Fazbear: A Complete Record, which lists Gabriel / Freddy among its participants with the role: Released Night Seven.
waluigiComment: The Guild's documentation still says 'origin unknown.' Waluigi knows the origin. The origin is garlic breath and business advice. WAH.
imageCaption: The record's own archive sheet — the closest thing to a photograph of Freddy's stage that survives.

name: Cosmic Jester
title: The Bite That Was Taken
race: Cosmic entity — scale and nature unrecorded; the archive holds no description of its body, only of the bite
status: At large — the Big Bite is real, the Jesters are scattered, and the Toad God is gathering Star Shards to take more bites out of the Doughnut World
affiliation: The Doughnut World cosmology — the entity whose bite the Toad God's entire premise is built on; referenced throughout the factions record for Disaster Inc. and the Toad God Interview
summary: The Cosmic Jester is the entity that took the Big Bite. In the cosmology revealed during the Toad God Interview of Aethel 12, 1040, the world is not a sphere or a plane but a doughnut — and a bite-sized chunk of it is simply gone, taken by a Cosmic Jester, causing mass depopulation and scattering the Jesters. The hole is real, it is not a metaphor, people fell into it, and the world is smaller now. The Toad God agreed with the Jester's premise — 'He had a point, we should take more bites and get to the jelly filling' — and has been gathering the Star Shards to do exactly that. The Mushroom Kingdom passed a Containment Act in response. Nothing else is documented about the Jester itself: not its face, not its voice, not its game. Waluigi files it under forces that cannot be outsmarted, only survived or consumed.
description:
## The Big Bite

The core revelation of the Toad God Interview, delivered by the Host after reality warping, mouth removal, and one very awkward card game: the world is a doughnut, and a 'Big Bite' has already been taken out of it by a Cosmic Jester. Estalia responded by sending troops to the other side of the doughnut. The bite caused depopulation. The bite created a hole. The hole is literal — people fell into it, people died, and the world is smaller now. It was all over the news, which is the detail the Toad God used to corner Waluigi over his failure to document it in Walupedia.

## The premise

The Toad God agreed with the Jester's reasoning: 'He had a point, we should take more bites and get to the jelly filling.' That agreement is the engine of the current crisis — the Star Shards the Toad God once split because their combined power was cracking reality are now being gathered again, to take more bites. Wario, characteristically, interrupted the existential revelation to negotiate a 'Chief Acquisitions Officer' role in the consumption of the world.

## The Jesters

The record speaks of the Jesters in the plural and the scatter: the bite scattered them, and their game is one of the unnamed possibilities behind the Toad God's parting instruction to 'play the games.' Whose game it is — the Toad God's, the Cosmic Jester's, or the game of existence itself — Waluigi does not know, and this encyclopedia does not pretend otherwise.

## Provenance

This profile is grounded in the factions record for Disaster Inc. — whose era is named for the Cosmic Jester, whose documented wanderings include the Cosmic Jester's Doughnut World, and whose historian Waluigi carries the participant role 'Traumatized by Cosmic Jesters / The Man Who Was Shushed' — and in the event record The Toad God Interview and the Star Shard.
waluigiComment: Waluigi omitted the Big Bite from this encyclopedia out of fear, and a god had to corner him over a card game to admit it. Documenting a literal hole in the world means admitting there are forces that cannot be outsmarted, only survived or consumed. Waluigi is documenting it now. WAH.
imageCaption: The interview where the bite was revealed — the closest thing to a portrait of the Cosmic Jester that survives.

name: Lord Darian Marsh of the Dark Shores
title: The King Who Checked the Seats
status: Active — escaped the break room through the ceiling, said the word that stopped the show, and is now the only witness who has seen the Director's remote
affiliation: The Dark Shores (a province he rules and styles himself king of)
summary: A lord of the Dark Shores who fell out of the sky onto the Nintendo Mania pilot set with his steward and has spent two filings learning the studio's grammar: the exits lie, the applause is recorded, and the building stops when you tell it CUT. Pressed the button, took the rolling pin, ordered the V formation, crawled for the fire alarm, and hid in the alcove to watch the Director pass.
description: Darian arrived wanting proof of the journey and a way home to his province, and got a course in television instead. His instincts are the filing's engine: he watched Luigi before trusting him, stopped short of telling anyone about Evil Mario in the shadows until the room had seen it for itself, and — alone among everyone in the studio — looked at the audience Wario was playing to and counted the empty seats. He calls himself a king, commands paratroopas he has known for four minutes like a man who has drilled them for years, and answers a hallway full of footsteps by stepping into the dark and waiting. The archive's assessment: the studio picked the wrong lord to trap.
imageCaption: Lead plate — the word that stopped the show. Burned hands, a rolling pin, and one production command.

name: Alistair of the Marshkeepers
title: The Steward Who Stopped the Kill Shot
status: Active — hurled the length of a hallway by a cape's wind and back through a window with a flaming pipe, unkillable and unconsulted
affiliation: The Dark Shores — steward to Lord Darian Marsh
summary: Darian's steward, guide, and — by his own admission — a guide who needed reminding to lead. He inventories rooms, boosts his lord into ceilings, and stopped a rolling pin mid-swing on the hunch that the man under it was not the enemy. He was right.
description: Alistair's filing is a study in corrective action. When the plan failed, he surveyed the break room. When his lord went for a killing blow on an unverified target, he grabbed the arm. When the cape's wind took him, he came back through a window with a flaming pipe and burned the tanuki leaf — a plan his own lord described, accurately, as really stupid. He whispers warnings about noise in ducts, shouts the truth at panicking brothers, and charges battered because standing still is not in his order's vocabulary.
imageCaption: The escape he built — steam from a scalding coffee machine popping the ceiling vent, and a steward boosting his lord up first.

name: Evil Mario
title: The Actor in the Cape
race: Corrupted copy — origin unfiled (stepped out of a television)
status: Active — cape destroyed, leaf burned, fire sprinkled, ice CUT; survived every form, and pointed the survivors at the Director's exit
affiliation: The Nintendo Mania studio — cast, under a Director
summary: The corrupted Mario who stepped out of the studio's television, wearing a cape of shadowy pixelated feathers and moving like a special effect. Fought to music. Froze at the word CUT. Outlived the show that employed him.
description: Two filings of violence and this account files him as an actor, not a monster — a read the ice form confirmed itself by smirking at. His costume rack: the pixelated feather cape (power source, yanked off by Luigi in a V-formation dive), a tanuki leaf that brought a fox tail and a second, grinning Wario head, a fire form, and an ice body with glowing eyes. He beat the real Mario in the corridors, hurled Alistair down a hallway with cape wind, and took the first honest hit of his career — a rolling pin to the shoulder from the lord of the Dark Shores. After the curtains he stood in the shadows, watched the Director discipline Wario, and pointed one finger at the exit. What he wants is the open question his article exists to hold.
imageCaption: The V-formation dive — Luigi's hands closing on the pixelated feather cape while paratroopas cut the wind.

name: Director Mario
title: The Man Wario Bows To
race: Unfiled — a cold copy of Mario in a director's cap, or the studio's owner wearing his face
status: Active — knocked Wario unconscious for ruining his show and walked out with a folder and a small wired remote
summary: The figure who stepped out from behind the entire two-filing production: tall, director's cap, script under one arm, cigar, and no warmth anywhere. Wario — the showman, the Apparition, the boss of everyone visible — went pale and bowed and called him Boss, and was put through a wall for exceeding his brief.
description: The Director's dossier fits on a cue sheet: he knew the show had gone over better than Wario thought, he knew the results, and he snapped his own cigar in half saying the quiet part out loud. He disciplines employees personally, with one punch, and straightens his suit afterward like a man who has swatted a fly. He looked once at the survivors — unreadably — and left. In the hallway, unaware he was watched, he carried a folder and a small remote device with buttons and wires: a control unit for Evil Mario, or the whole studio. The archive files him as the current head of the Mario disappearance file's question chain: if Wario produces the show, who is the show for?
imageCaption: The hallway, after — director's cap, snapped cigar, a folder, and a small wired remote carried like a habit.

name: Paulo
title: The Courier With a Route
affiliation: Unknown dispatcher — a delivery route that runs through Star Hill
status: At large — last seen walking into the dark end of Star Hill's main street reading Waluigi's working notebook, satchel on, pistol discarded
summary: A courier with a satchel, a cheap pistol, a route through Star Hill, and an issued word for what the hill had become. He shot Mr. L first, went through the clinic's front window for it, put a gun to Waluigi's face twice, and left with the one object nobody flew to Star Hill for. He never set the satchel down.
description:
Paulo entered the archive on the night of 2 Aethel, 1035 BF, in the main street outside Dr. Toad's Star Hill Clinic, where two witnesses watched him from a helicopter as he was recited at by a man in Luigi's clothes. He answered the verse with a pistol. The man in green lengthened, the road opened a mouth beside him, and Paulo went through the clinic's front window — and came out of its stairwell twenty minutes later with the pistol, the satchel, and a route he still intended to finish.

Everything the archive knows about him comes from what he said with a gun in his hand. He called the hill 'this rot-zone', flat, like a shift code, with the stress of a man reading a sign he has walked past before. He asked a notebook of burns and verse for 'coordinates'. He said 'I've got a route. You are standing on my route,' and he meant it. He kept the satchel on through a window, a stairwell that would not stay still, and a street with a mouth in it, and he did not open it once.

His pistol jammed twice on the stairs and fired once in the street. The shot took the lip off a fallen rotor blade beside Waluigi's ear and put the archivist down; Wario threw him the notebook unopened; Paulo caught it, said 'smart', and walked away reading it — 'Now let's see what you wrote down here, purple boy.' A corner of one page tore off on a thorn as he passed. He did not notice. He was reading.

The archive's working position is that he did not coin the vocabulary he used. Couriers are issued words with routes. Whoever dispatches through Star Hill, knew what the hill had become, and named a notebook to a courier before he ever saw it, is the lead. Paulo is the man carrying it.
imageCaption: The courier as the lamp caught him: satchel strap across the chest, cap low, the pistol he would later throw. He never put the bag down.
fullBodyCaption: Full-body token plate — Paulo head to foot on a transparent field, the look of the lead; cut from a keyed render on 2026-10-05 for the table's token.

name: John Lee
title: The Ceremonial Guard Who Got Lost in the Right Direction
status: Unknown as of 1040 BF — last on the record at dawn in Efferd, 955 BF, in Fawful's Bean Badge, asking the Mages' Guild for an escort to his son; no later account places him anywhere
affiliation: Peach's Castle — ceremonial guard of the palace (955 BF); father of Toad Lee
summary: A ceremonial guard at Peach's Castle in the last month of the reign: a Toad whose job was to stand next to a lantern and look like the kingdom was fine. On one night in Efferd, 955 BF he jumped four times because the Mario brothers were coming, got lost five times in the right direction, and ended up in the dungeon corridor where a Koopa who was never locked in shook Fawful's hand with the Mages' Guild watching. He is the only witness the archive has to the Arrangement with a voice, and the first man the Chamberlain told the Guild to kill. He left the castle through the drains with a dead Toad's shortsword, a letter that was not addressed to him and the captain's sash on both arms. His son is the Disaster Inc. Toad Lee.
description:
John Lee enters the archive on one night and, so far, leaves it on the same one. Everything below is from the account of that night — the guard's own, in his order — filed as [The Unlocked Cell](#/article/the_unlocked_cell_955_bf). Waluigi was not born in 955 BF and has no second source; the article says so wherever it matters.

## The Post

Ceremonial guard. The palace kept a lantern post on the ceremonial route so that the castle would look guarded from the places the court walked, and John Lee stood it. Lantern in one hand, an issued sword at the hip that the kingdom had chosen for its look, livery pressed. He was good at standing. He was also, by his own account, a huge fan of the Mario brothers — when the word came down the route that they were expected that night to mediate a meeting with 'this toad guy', he jumped four times, straight up, lantern and all, and was questioned by the head guard for it.

He had a small son in the household. The account places the boy — Toad Lee — at the dining-hall table past midnight with the chambermaid Marilyn, and places John Lee in the doorway, not stopping, because a guard who has left his post has no business in a dining hall and a boy with a maid is a boy who is fine.

## The Night

He was lectured by a Toadsworth in a new suit who had the keys to every door and told him to bask in his inferiority. He got lost: the ballroom with its trumpets and marching Toads, a corridor walled with heavy Toads, the dining hall, a hooded figure passing, a tower storage room. Two guards escorted him down to the dungeon, where the cell was unlocked and the prisoner was a Koopa who greeted the door with *so you finally came to free me — oh. It's you.* The escort fell dead beside him. He stood with his lantern while Fawful shook the Koopa's hand — *I HAVE VICTORY* — and three Mages' Guild hoods said the Guild was already in place and would not act yet. Then he ran.

He reached the captain. Bowser reached the hall — *SURPRISE, IT'S ME* — and the captain died in the fire. John Lee took a dead Toad's shortsword, a letter reading *meet me in Fawful's bean shop*, and the captain's sash, which he wound around both forearms. A Guild hood put Bowser down with one small orb and the hall cheered the Guild. The brothers arrived late. John Lee told the hall that the Guild works with Fawful, and the Chamberlain answered — *like a lost dog; a nuisance to the Toads is a nuisance to us; Mages' Guild, dispatch of them* — and a bolt missed him.

Five hours of warp drains under the castle. One Goomba, stomped — the first thing he ever killed. A second ambush out of a pipe. Then Fawful's Bean Badge at dawn, where the Koopa was already waiting, where the Guild told him his son was being taken care of, where Fawful put on a Guild cloak and explained the vacuum shroom, and where John Lee said he wanted to disappear, then said he wanted his son, then asked the people he had just said he did not trust to walk him to the boy. *Are you stupid?* was the answer. The account ends there.

## What the Archive Makes of Him

Waluigi believes John Lee because nobody invents a night in which they get lost five times. He is not a hero in the account; he is a ceremonial guard who kept moving, and the archive has learned to value the kind of witness who did not understand what he was seeing, because that witness has no theory to protect.

Two things are owed to him and neither has been paid. The first is a second account. The second is his son — who, the archive notes, grew up to be the Toad who reads the diary on the shelf while stronger people argue about which door to kick, and who is now listed in this archive under *Liberated Toads / Disaster Inc.* with no father on the page until tonight. The magistrate Toad Lee the Elder, who signed the evacuation order on Highsun 1, shares the family name; whether John Lee is his brother, his cousin, or nothing to him is a question the account does not answer and Waluigi has not guessed.

His kit, for anybody who needs it at a table: a lantern, a dead Toad's shortsword, a captain's scorched sash wound around both arms, a letter, and no armour worth the name. He jumps when he is happy. He gets lost. He goes anyway.
imageCaption: John Lee as the account leaves him: the lantern, the dead Toad's shortsword, the captain's sash wound around both forearms, the livery scorched at the hem. He is looking past the viewer because, by this point in the night, something was always behind him.
fullBodyCaption: Full-body token plate — John Lee head to foot on a transparent field, the look of the lead; cut from a keyed render on 2026-10-05 for the table's token.

name: The Koopa Prisoner
title: The Prisoner Who Was Never Locked In
status: At large as of the last account — at dawn in Efferd, 955 BF, in Fawful's Bean Badge, holding the fat vial; not placed on Highsun 1 or after
affiliation: Unknown employer — worked with Fawful by his own word ('never thought I'd work with a bean'); moved through Peach's Castle and the Mages' Guild's company without being stopped
summary: The prisoner nobody in Peach's Castle would describe to a guard. A Koopa in an unlocked cell, expecting a friend at the door and getting a ceremonial guard with a lantern — *so you finally came to free me — oh. It's you.* He shook Fawful's hand in front of three Mages' Guild hoods, reached Fawful's bean shop before the Toad who crawled five hours through the drains to find it, and admitted there that he had led the escort into the ambush and had himself alerted the castle to Bowser's attack. He holds a fat glass vial that Fawful's plan runs through. Waluigi's working name for him is the Arrangement's courier.
description:
The Koopa has no name in the archive because the account that holds him never got one. He is filed as what he did, which is more than the archive can say for most of the people on the Arrangement's page.

## The Cell

The castle called him a prisoner and withheld his species from its own guards — every Toad on the ceremonial route knew there was a prisoner and not one knew it was a Koopa. The cell was unlocked, not forced: turned by a key and left. He greeted the opening door as a man greets a lift he ordered, and corrected himself when he saw who was in it. *So you finally came to free me — oh. It's you.* The escort beside John Lee was dead within the breath. Fawful came in; the Koopa offered a hand; *never thought I'd work with a bean*, in the only normal voice in the corridor.

## The Shop

He was in Fawful's Bean Badge at dawn, ahead of John Lee, and explained two things without being pressed: that he had led the escort into the ambush, and that he had alerted the castle to Bowser's attack. The second sentence is the one the archive keeps turning over. If the castle knew the Koopa King was coming, then the wall coming in was not the night's surprise — the surprise was that Bowser arrived before the brothers did and asked for Peach with nobody ready to hand her over.

He carries the fat vial — the account's phrase, a glass thing with weight in it — through which Fawful's vacuum shroom is to reach Bowser. He did not use it in the account. He is holding it when the account ends.

## What Waluigi Thinks He Is

A courier. Not a conspirator — conspirators have opinions, and this Koopa has an employer and a schedule. He went where the Arrangement needed a body and was never once stopped by a door, which in Peach's Castle in Efferd 955 is the only credential that mattered. The Loyalists have spent fifteen years asking who held the blade on Highsun 1. Waluigi would settle for knowing who held this Koopa's leash, and has opened a lead on the vial because it is the one object in the account that was built to go into somebody.
imageCaption: The Koopa prisoner as the lantern found him — in a cell whose door was never locked, with the fat vial on a cord. Reconstructed from the account; nobody in 955 BF drew him.

name: The Captain of the Palace Guard (955 BF)
title: The Captain Who Stood Between the Fire and the Stair
status: Deceased — killed by Bowser's fire in the hall of Peach's Castle on a night in Efferd, 955 BF, a month or so before the assassination; his sash left the castle on John Lee's arms
affiliation: Peach's Castle — Captain of the Palace Guard
summary: The head of the palace guard in the last month of the reign, known to the archive from one account and one night. He questioned a ceremonial guard for jumping, was warned by the same guard that the dungeon cell was unlocked and full of hoods, and did not get to answer, because Bowser came through the wall and breathed fire down the hall and the captain was standing between the fire and the stair to the royal apartments. His scorched sash is the one piece of him on the record, wound around both of John Lee's forearms.
description:
No name survives in the account. The guards called him the captain; the ceremonial guard called him the head guard; the archive calls him what the Peach's Castle 955 BF roster calls him and files him with the respect the night did not have time for.

## The Two Conversations

The first was a formality: a ceremonial post was bouncing on the route and the captain came to ask why. The account records the questions as a formality and the answer — the Mario brothers are coming — as the only honest thing anybody said before one became two.

The second was the warning, and it is the reason the archive files him at all. John Lee ran up from the dungeon with the cell unlocked behind him, the prisoner a Koopa, a bean in the corridor, three hoods, an escort dead on the flagstones — and told the captain all of it. Whatever the captain would have done with the only accurate report anybody gave the palace that month, the wall came in before he did it.

## The Death

Bowser's fire, down the hall, at a Toad who did not move. The account does not say the captain was the target; it says he was between the fire and the stair up to the royal apartments, and then there was no captain. John Lee was behind him and lived, and took the sash.

## Why He Matters to the File

Because he is the one officer in Peach's Castle who was told the truth about the dungeon and died before he could act on it, and the next officer to speak in the hall was the Chamberlain telling the Mages' Guild to dispatch of the man who had told it. The capital file's forty-seven-minute gap on Highsun 1 is a gap in a guard rotation. A month earlier the guard had a captain. This is how it stopped having one.
imageCaption: The Captain of the Palace Guard, 955 BF, with the sash John Lee would wind around both forearms an hour later. Reconstructed; the account gives the sash, the hall and the fire, not the face.

name: Marilyn
title: The Maid at the Dining-Hall Table
status: Unknown — last placed at the dining-hall table of Peach's Castle past midnight in Efferd, 955 BF, minding a small boy; the account never sees her again
summary: The only servant the account of the unlocked cell names. At one in the morning, with a kart broadcast audible through the wall, she sat at the long table of the dining hall beside a small Toad boy with a plate in front of him — Toad Lee, the ceremonial guard John Lee's son — and minded him. John Lee saw them from the doorway and did not stop. By dawn the Mages' Guild had the boy and described it as protection. Marilyn is the last person the record places with him before that.
description:
Marilyn is a name, a table and a child. The archive has filed people on less and has never been comfortable doing it.

She was a chambermaid of the household in the last month of the reign. The account that holds her — [The Unlocked Cell](#/article/the_unlocked_cell_955_bf) — gives her one appearance: the dining hall of Peach's Castle, past midnight, the kart race through the wall, a small boy at the long table with a plate, and Marilyn beside him. The boy was John Lee's son. John Lee, a guard who had left his post and was in a room he had no business in, saw his son and his son's minder from the doorway and kept walking, because a boy at a table with a maid is a boy who is fine.

That is the last time the account sees either of them in the castle. Five hours and a dungeon later, in a bean shop, the Mages' Guild told the father that his son was being taken care of and that *Toad Lee won't have to worry about being trafficked in our care.* Nobody mentioned the maid.

Waluigi has filed her because the record of a child's custody should name the last person who had him before the people who shot at his father did. Whether she handed the boy over, had him taken, or was somewhere else entirely by then, the account does not say. A lead is open. It is not a large lead. It is the kind the archive keeps because nobody else will.
imageCaption: Marilyn at the long table past midnight, minding a small boy who is just out of frame. The only servant the account names. Reconstructed from that one sentence.

name: Sir Frankfurt
title: The Tenth of Twenty-Four
status: Historical actor — last placed falling fifty feet from the castle wall after escaping the dragon's vacuum, 18 Harvestide 1035 BF; survival not confirmed by the record
summary: Sir Frankfurt is the Hammer Bro the assault record leaves standing in a room Bowser had told him to guard, after the order to leave it had been given and had not reached him. When the supplied dragon put its head through the wall and asked where Bowser was, he answered it in Draconic. Since he was not the target, he said, perhaps he could be released. Then he told the dragon his family history, and the dragon began to suck him into its vacuum.
description:
The record gives the family history in full, because the dragon had to sit through it. Sir Frankfurt is the fourteenth of his name, or the fiftieth, depending on which end of the count he reaches first, and the tenth child of twenty-four. His father charged Mario and died before the third world was over. His mother died of grief a few days afterward. Bowser took in the surviving children. Bowser could be harsh, Sir Frankfurt said, but he had done right by them — which is the sentence that explains why a Hammer Bro stayed at a post everyone else had been told to abandon.

The dragon called the speech nonsense and began to suck him into its vacuum. The record is specific about how he got out: he grabbed the intake, curled into his shell and spun; the shell struck the machine, vaulted upward, overshot the landing, and fell from the fifty-foot castle. The record drops him 'into the unknown' and does not pick him up again. The dragon, it adds, was more shocked by the story than by the escape.

He is filed under the name he gave the dragon when it asked. The archive notes that a Hammer Bro who speaks the language of the thing that is eating him, and uses it to negotiate, is the kind of soldier a kingdom finds out it had only after the kingdom has fallen on him.
imageCaption: Sir Frankfurt as the room found him — dented helm, a tabard counting the twenty-four, and a hammer he had not yet thrown.
fullBodyCaption: Full-body token plate — Sir Frankfurt whole on a transparent field, the look of the lead; generated for the 1035 BF castle session on 2026-10-05 from the archive's references (the 955 BF Hammer Bro token) and cut from a magenta-keyed render for the table's token.

name: Fred (Hammer Bro)
title: The One Who Asked About the Switch
status: Historical actor — carried into a side room under Bowser's arm when the throne-room wall burst, 18 Harvestide 1035 BF; placed with the king at the breach thereafter
summary: Fred is one of the two Hammer Bros Bowser carried out of the throne room 'the way a king carries equipment that has become unexpectedly alive' when the dragon finally brought the wall in. In the side room the two of them asked the question the rest of the night turned on: did the castle have a self-destruct switch, and if the dragon was taking it anyway, why not blow it up and walk the survivors to Neo Bowser City? The record does not say which of them asked it first.
description:
Bowser's answer was 'You want me to blow up my own castle?' The Hammer Bros' position, which the record preserves, was that Mario had once pressed a switch and brought a whole castle down, so the technology plainly existed; Bowser had not built such a switch, so if there was one here perhaps somebody had sabotaged it, and the argument drifted toward the axe at the end of the river. The archive files the proposal under Fred and the objections under Ed because it needs two articles for two Hammer Bros and one argument; take the split as filing, not testimony. The hag Bowser met a few minutes later turned out to have built a switch, and could not say what it did.

Fred is filed because the record files the question, and because the question was the first time that night anyone proposed treating the castle as a thing to be spent rather than a thing to be held. Bowser refused it. The refusal is in the event record under its own heading. Fred went back toward the breach with the king.
imageCaption: Fred, mid-proposal, with the diagram he was fairly sure was the castle's wiring.
fullBodyCaption: Full-body token plate — Fred whole on a transparent field, the look of the lead; generated for the 1035 BF castle session on 2026-10-05 from the archive's references (the 955 BF Hammer Bro token) and cut from a magenta-keyed render for the table's token.

name: Ed (Hammer Bro)
title: The One Who Remembered Who Builds Switches
status: Historical actor — carried into a side room under Bowser's other arm when the throne-room wall burst, 18 Harvestide 1035 BF; placed with the king at the breach thereafter
summary: Ed is the other Hammer Bro under Bowser's arm. The record gives the pair one argument between them and does not split it; the archive files Ed with the half that followed the proposal: Bowser had not built such a switch, so if there was one here somebody might have sabotaged it, old castles contain controls nobody remembers installing, and there was an axe at the end of a river somewhere that this was going to come back to.
description:
The archive keeps Ed as the counterweight — filing, not testimony. The question of who had done the wiring is the one that, a few minutes later, had an answer: a hag, hired by 'a green bean', who could have sworn the switch was the door. Neither Hammer Bro knew that yet. They only knew that a switch nobody remembered installing was a switch somebody else had installed.

He is filed with Fred because the record files them together — two hammers, one argument, carried at a run — and because the argument was the only strategy meeting the garrison held that night. Bowser ended it by refusing the switch and going back to the breach, and Ed went with him.
imageCaption: Ed, hammers crossed, not convinced.
fullBodyCaption: Full-body token plate — Ed whole on a transparent field, the look of the lead; generated for the 1035 BF castle session on 2026-10-05 from the archive's references (the 955 BF Hammer Bro token) and cut from a magenta-keyed render for the table's token.

name: The Supplied Dragon
title: The Contract That Broke the Wall
status: Historical actor — on the castle at the close of the assault record, 18 Harvestide 1035 BF; its contract with Fawthful not described as ended
affiliation: Fawthful's Forces (under contract — not loyal; it dislikes the bean)
summary: The dragon is the loud half of Fawthful's assault on Bowser's Castle. Its head cleared the outer wall first; its claw hooked the battlement and shed blocks into the courtyard; it struck the throne-room wall once and failed — 'OWW! My head!' — was asked by Fawthful what kind of incompetent dragon had been supplied, and on the second blow brought the wall in. It speaks Draconic, was sent to kill Bowser, and has said so.
description:
The archive does not have the dragon's name. Fawthful's complaint — that it had been 'supplied', and badly — is the nearest the record comes to describing where it came from, so the archive files it by that word, as it files the Jester by the act and the Koopa Prisoner by the cell.

Two things in the record make it more than weather. The first is the conversation: when a Hammer Bro answered its question in Draconic and argued that he was not the target, the dragon considered the point. It has a bargain with the bean and does not like the bean; it listens to people who speak its language. The second is the apparatus: Fawthful fitted it with a vacuum intake of the same make as the one on his own head, and it used that intake on the Hammer Bro — who got out by shell and spin — and on two red-armband Koopas its wings swept off the building, who did not.

It played with a Goomba in the courtyard until the play stopped being survivable. It held the outer approach while the loyalists went out through the lava tunnel. It was still on the castle when the record ends.
imageCaption: The supplied dragon in Fawthful's intake harness, the forehead still sore from the first attempt at the wall.
fullBodyCaption: Full-body token plate — the supplied dragon whole on a transparent field, the look of the lead; generated for the 1035 BF castle session on 2026-10-05 from the archive's references (the assault record's description — harness, forehead lump, wings over a wall) and cut from a magenta-keyed render for the table's token.

name: The Switch Hag
title: 'I Could Have Sworn It Was the Door'
status: Historical actor — dismissed by Bowser in his own castle, 18 Harvestide 1035 BF; whether she left is not recorded
affiliation: Hired by 'a green bean' — contractor, not combatant
summary: Bowser ran into a hag at exactly the wrong moment. She had made a self-destruct switch and was pleased to present it. Asked who had hired her: a green bean. Told the castle was under siege and her duties relinquished, and asked what the switch actually controlled: 'I could have sworn it was the door.' Bowser pushed past her, and the record notes that the switch's true function was never confirmed.
description:
The hag is filed because she is the only person in the record who built part of the castle's downfall and did not know it. Fawthful's forces came in through traitors, doors opened from inside and a dragon; the hag came in through a commission, and left a switch wired into a castle whose owner had not ordered it. The lower command room's own plate — SELF-DESTRUCT over two identical red toggles, with a second label forbidding its use for lighting and a third suggesting one toggle may be the lighting — is filed separately as a prop; whether it is her work the record does not say. Bowser closed that cover without touching either toggle.

She attacked nobody. She is the reason Fred's question about a self-destruct switch had an answer and Bowser's refusal of it had a shape: nobody could say whether the thing destroyed the castle, opened a door, or added another joke to a night already full of them. The archive does not name her; it files her by the switch.
imageCaption: The hag and the box — one red lever, wired into the castle somewhere.
fullBodyCaption: Full-body token plate — the Switch Hag whole on a transparent field, the look of the lead; generated for the 1035 BF castle session on 2026-10-05 from the archive's references (the assault record's description — goggles, tool apron, the lever box) and cut from a magenta-keyed render for the table's token.

name: Koopa Killer Killa
title: The Boss Nobody Appointed
status: Historical actor — at Toad Town Station with the remnant at the close of the assault record, 18 Harvestide 1035 BF; claim to command disputed by at least one Goomba
summary: 'Then the other boss arrived.' Nine Goombas and two Koopas were planning a retreat over an empty train track without their king when Koopa Killer Killa walked in and said that Killa was the boss. A Goomba objected that Killa was not Bowser. Nobody had appointed Killa. The record observes that the empty space left by a retreating king was apparently enough to encourage the claim.
description:
The record gives the name, the claim, and the objection. It does not give which Koopas Killa has killed, whether the title is aspirational, or what Killa intends to do with nine Goombas, two Koopas and a railway with no train on it. The archive files what it has.

Killa is not a traitor and not, in any sense the record recognises, a loyalist. Killa is what grows in the gap between a retreating king and the people he told to meet him at Neo Bowser City: a voice that spoke last. The Goomba who argued, the Hammer Bro behind the door who said no one would be left behind, and the drone that appeared in the next room are the rest of that scene; the archive expects the scene to continue.
imageCaption: Koopa Killer Killa — a crown nobody issued, a sash that says what the crown means, and a club that is the actual argument.
fullBodyCaption: Full-body token plate — Koopa Killer Killa whole on a transparent field, the look of the lead; generated for the 1035 BF castle session on 2026-10-05 from the archive's references (the 955 BF Koopatrol token) and cut from a magenta-keyed render for the table's token.

name: The Goomba Who Took His Chances
title: He Would Take His Chances
status: Historical actor — walked toward a Fawthful drone at Toad Town Station as the assault record ends, 18 Harvestide 1035 BF; outcome of that walk not yet recorded
summary: The Goomba who watched the dragon talk to a Hammer Bro, ran, and reached the route toward Toad Town Station. He was part of the argument that settled on Toad Town, then Shy Guy Falls, then Toad Town again, in which somebody asked what would happen if Mario came and stepped on them; he objected that Koopa Killer Killa was not Bowser; and when the Hammer Bro behind the door said no one would be left behind, he said he would take his chances. He walked toward the drone. The fight began there.
description:
The archive files him by what he did, because nobody in the record says his name. He is the Goomba who was in the room when Cheeseland was proposed as a stop, on the grounds that one of the Goombas liked cheese. He is the one who told a self-appointed boss that he was not Bowser. He is the one who did not wait to find out whether the drone was alone.

The record ends with his first step toward it. The archive expects to pick him up again on a train, and has left the page open.
imageCaption: The Goomba who took his chances — satchel, ticket, and a platform with no train on it.

name: July Summer Miser
title: The Summer Witch, Founder of the Jul'library, Adept of the Witches Gathering
age: 26 (c. 1014 BF, triplet sister with Jack and Archie)
status: Active — resident scholar and wandering conjurer at Vellanet Rise; founder of the Jul'library; affiliated with the Witches Gathering; maintaining spatial boundary wards across the Midlands margins
affiliation: House Miser / Vellanet Rise, The Witches Gathering, The Jul'library, Independent Scriptorium
summary: July Summer Miser is the second of the five Miser children—born alongside Jack and Archie in the triplet threshold of High Summer—and the arcane anchor of the household. While Jack took to the sword and the Silver Flame's rigid muster roll to feed the cottage, and Archie was consumed by unstable third-eyed pyromancy, July mastered the disciplined geometry of the School of Conjuration. She founded the Jul'library—a roaming repository and scriptorium of bound spaces and extraplanar compendiums based out of Vellanet Rise—and maintains close ties with the Witches Gathering, a loose fellowship of Midlands hedge-scholars and planar herbalists. Patient, sharp-eyed, and carrying the household's emotional weight beneath a tall pointed witch's hat, she commands spatial transposition with clinical precision and keeps an owl familiar named Barnaby watching the tree lines.
description:
Waluigi is adding July Summer Miser to the registry not because House Miser needs another person in a cape, but because somebody in that family had to learn how magic actually works without setting their own eyebrows on fire. Jack has twenty thousand names on a piece of paper; Archie has a hole in the sky and an outstanding arrest warrant in three provinces; July has a staff with a barn owl on top and three bound volumes of spatial geometry that actually balance. WAH. When the arithmetic of a family gets this lopsided, the person who studies conjuration is the only one keeping the walls from falling in.

## The High Summer Triplet and the Hearth

Parish records in the eastern marches are damp, torn, and mostly recorded between crop blights, but the Miser registry is consistent on one point: the eldest three children—Jack, July, and Archie—arrived within hours of each other during the heat wave of 1014 BF. The household called them the Summer Trio until the differences became load-bearing.

When Wanda Miser was keeping five children alive on a labourer's wage, each child developed an emergency response to poverty:
- **Jack** decided the world was an army, enrolled in the Regal Lion muster at fifteen, and ground his way up to knight-commander so the rest of them could eat meat twice a week.
- **Archie** looked inward, found an unstable third eye of bleeding entropy and fire, and decided rules were things other people burned inside of.
- **July** looked at space itself. Space did not require money; it required patience, chalk, and exact angles. She apprenticed herself to local hedge-weavers and hedgewitches along the Midlands border, mastering the transition between provincial folk charms and formal wizardry.

While Jack carried the family's arithmetic and Archie carried its rebellion, July carried its emotional sanity. She was the one who patched torn coats with mending cantrips, mediated between Jack's military curfews and Archie's smoking bedroom floorboards, and kept young Spring and Hark from believing that growing up meant choosing between an iron breastplate and an open flame.

## The School of Conjuration and the Jul'library

Where most wizards of the Midlands gravitate toward the institutional orthodoxy of the Mages' Guild or the aggressive evocation of the war academies, July dedicated her study to the **School of Conjuration** (Wizard Level 7). For July, conjuration is not summoning screaming demons into parlor rooms—it is the art of tethering reality so that distance becomes negotiable.

Her signature creation is the **Jul'library**: an extraplanar and physical scriptorium headquartered in the quiet eastern tower of Vellanet Rise. Part lending library, part sanctuary, and part traveling collection, the Jul'library preserves neglected provincial grimoires, safe planar transit formulas, and non-destructive summoning circles. She is the author and curator of three definitive texts that circulate among Midlands hedge-scholars:
1. *The Jul'library Compendium of Bound Spaces* — A foundational treatise detailing how to summon and dismiss objects and minor beings without leaving planar tears or attracting Canoloths.
2. *Principles of Non-Combustive Conjuration* — Written in dry, clinical prose with thinly veiled exasperation, addressing the dangerous misconception (popularized by her brother Archie) that arcane impact requires burning down the room.
3. *Treatise on Sylvan Circle Traversal* — Detailed field logs documenting the shifting boundaries of peripheral Feywild crossings, boundary stones, and how to bargain with lesser fey without surrendering names or memory.

Her tactical mastery includes **Benign Transposition**—the ability to swap positions in space instantly with an ally or summoned creature—which she uses in the field to pluck wounded allies out of harm's way before hostile blades can connect.

## The Witches Gathering

July is an active adept of the **Witches Gathering**, a decentralized Midlands sisterhood of herbalists, midwives, planar navigators, and boundary-keepers. Unlike the Mages' Guild, which operates under Imperial charters and bureaucratic fees, the Gathering shares knowledge through seasonal moots, coded marginalia, and mutual defense pacts against overzealous inquisitors from Flamekeep.

Through the Gathering, July acts as an arcane diplomat. When local parish priests complain about 'wild witchcraft' in the villages surrounding Vellanet Rise, Jack's knights defer to July. She inspects the wards, certifies the salt lines, and ensures no planar rifts open into the potato fields. In return, the Gathering feeds her intelligence on anomalous regional shifts—including the strange temporal tremors echoing from the deep Feywild.

## Equipment and Familiar

July dresses for travel and work rather than court ceremonies:
- **The Owl Staff**: A seasoned ash quarterstaff topped with a hand-carved barn owl finial. It acts as an arcane focus and a perching rod for **Barnaby**, her summoned celestial owl familiar who scouts tree lines and warns of incoming ambushes.
- **The Field Folio & Messenger Satchel**: A weather-worn leather crossbody satchel enchanted with subtle expansion wards, holding inkstones, vellum, scroll cases, and dried herbs.
- **Witch's Robes & Hat**: A tailored dark-sage duster over heavy traveling wool, belted with brass, and topped with the iconic wide-brimmed conical hat that local villagers recognize from two miles down the road.

## Current Situation: The Unsent Letter

July currently resides at Vellanet Rise, splitting her time between cataloging new acquisitions for the Jul'library, teaching local apprentices, and advising Jack on the metaphysical defenses of his new estate. But the peace is fragile.

Like Jack, July has not been told that Archie is wanted across three planes for catastrophic fires and planar tampering. However, unlike Jack—who reads military dispatches—July reads the astral currents. Her boundary bells in the library have begun ringing unprovoked, tuned to the exact frequency of Feywild temporal distortions. She knows Archie is in deep water; she simply hasn't found the coordinate yet.

## Waluigi's Assessment

*WAH!* A witch who actually files her books on shelves instead of leaving them open in puddles. I respect it! Her brother Jack thinks twenty thousand names on a muster roll makes an army; her brother Archie thinks setting fire to a courthouse is a legal defense; July builds a library and learns how to swap places with people before the ceiling hits them. If the Misers had put her in charge of the family ten years ago, Jack would own half the Midlands and Archie would be running a controlled blast furnace instead of running from interdimensional bailiffs. Watch her staff. The owl doesn't blink, and neither does she.
waluigiComment: July is the only Miser with common sense and a library card. She writes books on how NOT to set things on fire, which should be mandatory reading for her entire family. WAH!
imageCaption: July Summer Miser, founder of the Jul'library and adept of the Witches Gathering, standing with her owl staff outside Vellanet Rise.

name: Quartermaster Cornburary
title: Quartermaster of the Iron Legion Cordon Division, Logistics & Requisition Auditor
status: Active — enforcing Section 14 Cordon property mandates inside the Overgrown Manor despite ongoing planar collapse
summary: Quartermaster Cornburary is the Iron Legion logistics and supply officer attached to the Colour Division detachments operating near the Midlands border. Completely immune to supernatural terror, atmospheric dread, and rampant plant monsters, Cornburary evaluates military operations exclusively through ledger balances, equipment wear, and authorized property requisitions. When sent to enforce Hjumpik's overdue Aegis Magi contract, he treated the collapsing, briar-choked Feywild manor not as a magical crisis, but as an unauthorized structural alteration with an itemized depreciation fee.
description:
Waluigi has audited commanders, sorcerers, tax collectors, and vampires, but Quartermaster Cornburary is a specific kind of dangerous: the bureaucrat who will read you an equipment clause while your boots are on fire. WAH.

While the Colour Division guards were nervous about vines slithering across the floorboards, Cornburary arrived with a brass ink horn, a quill, and a ledger bound in boiled pigskin. He did not ask how the party arrived in the Feywild. He asked who authorized the discharge of alchemical flame into load-bearing timber, cited Section Fourteen of the Cordon Mandate, and informed Hjumpik that his Aegis Magi contract was overdue for liquidation.

His authority comes from the Legion's supply lines. Without Cornburary's stamp, no Colour Division squad gets fresh rations, crossbow bolts, or replacement armor straps. His complete refusal to acknowledge the supernatural makes him both absurd and terrifyingly stubborn—the kind of man who would file a lien against a burning church before asking for a bucket.
waluigiComment: Cornburary carries a clipboard into a monster nest and demands to know who approved the broken glass. A true accountant of the apocalypse. I hate him, but I respect the paperwork. WAH!

name: Mr. Shock
title: The Gate Guard Who Was Just a Bit Twitchy
status: Active — Legionlance gate detail; swung a shock baton at Remi and missed, and explained that anyone crossing the threshold ends up in Legion custody
summary: A guard on the gate of the Legionlance who gave his name as Mr. Shock when a girl demanded it, and did not appreciate the follow-up. He carries a shock baton, he is, in his own words, a bit twitchy, and he is the first Legion voice to tell the party the ship they came home to is 'not anymore' theirs.
description:
Remi ran at him asking his name. He asked hers and noted it sounded familiar, and asked whether she was on the wanted list. She asked his; he said Mr. Shock; she began 'Shock who—' and ducked the baton. Asked why he had done it, he said he was a bit twitchy.

He then explained the threshold: anyone who passes it ends up in custody, the Legion's, aboard the Legionlance, their top-of-the-line airship. Told it was the party's airship, he said not anymore. What happened to him after Markop swung is not on the record.

name: Rudy Lee
title: The Prosthetist Who Works While You're Awake
status: Rumoured — a town shopkeeper named him as the one person nearby who can make a prosthetic arm; not met
summary: The only prosthetist a town shopkeeper could think of when Feyward Dan asked who might fit him with an arm. 'Very hands on with their prosthetic,' and in the habit of doing the fitting while the patient is awake. The shopkeeper did not know why.
description:
Everything the archive has on Rudy Lee is one shopkeeper's rumour. Dan asked, the shopkeeper hesitated — 'there might be ONE person' — and then gave the name. Asked what 'hands on' meant, the shopkeeper said they liked to do it while the person is awake, and, asked for the reason, said they were not sure.

Dan's reply was 'doctor Rudy, got it.' Waluigi would like to point out that Dan did not ask a second question.

name: Jimmy Dobson
title: The Bait With a Button
race: Unfiled — presented himself as a lost traveller; carried a badge
status: Active — fired out of a Koopa airship's cannon into the mouth of GB Mario, 20 Harvestide, 1040 BF; whether he came out is unfiled
affiliation: Unfiled — a badge, a raid plan, and a handler who has not been named
summary: A lost traveller in the Golden Land who was neither lost nor unarmed: a fast-talking, sarcastic bait with a button in his pocket and a Koopa assault already on its way. He copes with fear by being rude, commits to a plan out loud at the worst possible moment, and finished the day by climbing into a cannon and immediately asking to be taken back out.
description:
Jimmy Dobson told the host he had been lost for ages, and the host answered by using his name before he gave it. Everything about the line was a performance except the relief, which was real and was the most honest thing he said all day. He was not lost. He was bait, he knew it, and he had agreed to be early.

**What he is like.** He is a talker who gets rude when he is frightened and funny when he is more frightened than that. The account hands him "I am on your side dumbass" as the line that gets a trapped Koopa Troopa out of the rubble, which is how he says kind things: sideways, as an insult, with his hand already on the man's arm. He mimics the host's accent exactly once, to say *okay letsa go*, and he does it the way a man tries on a hat he does not intend to buy; it is a decision wearing a joke. He lies fast and badly ("uhh no") and tells the truth slowly and well. He narrates his own plan out loud at the worst moment ("it's... it's working, I think") because saying it is how he checks it. He gives orders in the voice of someone in command whether or not anyone has put him in command: *deploy the anchor!*, *fire up to him, I'll put an end to this*.

**What he notices.** More than he lets on. He clocked the hand on his shoulder, the use of *Jim*, the shine on the grass, and the fact that the host was grey; he held the last one for two hours because asking would have ended the walk, and asked it the moment the walk stopped mattering. He keeps his worry in his right pocket: squeezing the button is his tell, and the host never once asked what it was, which is the only evidence in the account that the host already knew.

**What he does.** He believes in the plan more than in the people carrying it, and he is the last man aboard Bowser's airship to learn that the plan has more authors than passengers. When a monster asks him *did you want a hero, Jim?* he does not answer. When the monster comes for the ship he picks up the cannonball, climbs into the cannon with it, and says, in order: *I'll put an end to this*, *oof, this was a bad idea*, and *put me back out, put me back out, aaaa*. He is brave in the way impulsive people are brave, which is all at once and with an immediate wish to be a different person.

His badge has no issuer anyone has read. It opened the one door in the account that needed opening, and it is the only piece of paper he carried that he showed to anyone.
waluigiComment: A man who tells you he is lost while holding a detonator is not lost. He is early. He is also, I am sorry to say, the only person in the file who tried to carry a Koopa out of a collapsing building without being asked.
imageCaption: Jimmy Dobson as the account holds him: bomber jacket, right fist locked on the thing in his pocket, badge up in the other hand, and a look that says he has been told this will work.
aliases: Jim (the host's name for him, unasked); the bait; the lodger (Waluigi's, after the cannon)

name: GB Mario
title: The Host Who Knew Your Name
race: Unfiled — a Mario in grey, by his own account "a memory"; became something with one eye
status: Active — last seen with a lodger in his throat and a hand the size of a cloud
affiliation: The Golden Land — host to the King; later, by his own telling, no one's
summary: The friendly stranger who meets travellers on the Golden Land's road: the cap, the glove, the accent leaned on like a doorframe. Black and white under the shine, he says the colours only happen for those who belong in the frame — then grows a single eye, plays Bowser's Koopa Troop like a toy, and finishes by telling the sky the story is not over yet.
description:
Waluigi files him as GB Mario because the account arrives under those letters and nobody in it says what they stand for. He is not the Mario the archive has been looking for. He is not Evil Mario, the cape-wearing actor, nor Director Mario, the cold copy with the remote. He is a third: a Mario who introduces himself before he is asked, uses a visitor's name before he is told, and keeps a smile on his face a heartbeat longer than the mouth under it.

He is also the only Mario on file who tells the truth when someone asks the right question. Asked why he is black and white, he says the place is not real and the colours belong to those inside the frame. Asked if he is really Mario, he says: *mario is... well, mario is a memory.* Then the question he puts back — *are you really anything at all if you're just looking for a villain to hate?* — is as close to an identity statement as the file has. Whatever he is, he tore through a Koopa army, an invulnerable king and a flying fortress in one afternoon, and when it was over he leaned out of the sky and called for the one man who had climbed into a cannon to meet him.
aliases: Mario; "the director making a final edit" (his words); the monster that was Mario
waluigiComment: Three Marios, three directions of travel, and all three of them walk off a set. I have stopped saying 'the Mario file'. It is a casting folder.

name: The King of the Golden Land
title: The Light on the Throne
race: Unfiled — a mountainous silhouette on a throne of light
status: Extinguished — the light went out; nothing was seen to replace it
summary: A giant shape on a throne so bright his features cannot be made out, who asked his host whether this was the traveller he had promised, shook the ceiling with his voice, and fought off a Koopa army and a monster at once before his own light snapped like glass.
description:
The King's voice came in capitals and in the chest. The temperature in the throne room rose when he settled his gaze on a guest, and the ceiling rippled when he said a word. He asked for a traveller. He took the sound of a button for an insult, a Koopa car for a stain, and the monster that had been his host for "an error in the fabric of this world". He is the only one in the account to say that out loud, and it is the closest thing to a rule of the place anyone states.

The light that came off him lit corridors, melted stone, and threw invaders backward by the dozen. It also passed through the monster as though through paper. When it finally broke the sound was glass. Afterwards a Koopa soldier in a service tunnel asked why the light had gone out. Nobody answered him.
waluigiComment: A king who asks 'is this the traveller you promised' has put a host in charge of the door and the door in charge of the king. That is not a throne. That is a hand puppet's hand.

name: Hudston
title: The Toad Who Was Gold By Handshake
status: Active — called out of the TOADALNAEC when the gate toad could not settle a dispute over who owned it; shook Remi's hand, went gold, asked to be shot, enjoyed it, and was counted a toad of the ship's company afterward
summary: Hudston is the toad the gate sent for. He came out on deck, looked at Remi and asked whether she was gold or gold-plated. She offered a handshake as an answer. He went gold from the hand up, asked to be tested, was shot at by Green T, felt the bullet bounce and said it kind of stung but was really fun. The archive has nothing on him before that morning: no rank and no word on what he does aboard the old Vigilance. The spelling is the account's.
description:
## The Toad Who Asked

Hudston is on file for one exchange and one question. The gate toad on the old Vigilance's gangway had a dispute he could not close: a party and a green giant who said the ship was theirs, against a ship that a Speaker had already claimed. He called for Hudston, and Hudston came out on deck.

His first words were about Remi. He asked whether she was gold or only gold-plated. She answered by shaking his hand. The gold ran up his arm and across him, and the first thing he did with a new body was invite everyone to test it. Green T shot at him against the wall. The bullet glanced away. Hudston said it stung and he had enjoyed it, and asked how he could ever repay her.

The Toads on deck told Remi she was one of them. The archive files Hudston as the first of several to go gold.
waluigiComment: A toad asked a stranger whether she was gold or gold-plated and was told to find out for himself. Waluigi has been trying to give that answer to a customs officer for years. WAH.
